data.title: Pyrefly: A new type checker and IDE experience for Python
data.author: homarp
data.article_summary: Pyrefly是一款开源的Python类型检查工具和IDE扩展，使用Rust开发。它通过静态代码分析确保类型一致性，帮助在代码运行前发现错误，支持IDE集成和命令行使用。Pyrefly源于Instagram大规模代码库的需求，继承自Pyre类型检查器，但为了更高性能和更好的IDE体验而重新构建。其核心原则包括高性能、IDE优先、类型推断和开源合作。Pyrefly旨在实现实时代码检查、提升开发者体验，并与Python社区共同改进语言和类型系统。目前处于Alpha版本，欢迎社区反馈和贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Pyrefly（Meta推出的Python类型检查工具）的发布及其相关讨论，包括其竞争、实现语言、功能以及与现有工具的比较。

不同观点：
• **对Meta团队的担忧**（lacker）：担心Pyrefly可能像Meta之前的项目（如Atom或Flow）一样，被外部开源版本超越，从而使内部团队显得多余。建议相关负责人关注这一风险。

• **Pyrefly团队的回应**（team_pyrefly）：Pyrefly团队成员提供了官方FAQ链接，并表示愿意解答问题，试图缓解社区的疑问。

• **多个竞争者**（ThePhysicist）：目前有至少三个基于Rust的Python类型检查器（微软、Facebook、Astral），此外还有mypy。竞争激烈。

• **对Rust作为实现语言的质疑**（doug_durham）：质疑为何使用Rust实现Python工具是重要特性，认为对于非性能关键代码，使用Python编写更有利于社区支持和扩展。

• **Pyrefly的使用体验**（lucas_membrane）：用户在使用Pyrefly时遇到严格性超过Python本身的问题，但对工具发现其他问题表示肯定。同时讨论了使用SQLite管理数据流的方法是否合理。

• **编辑器集成**（xwowsersx）：对Pyrefly支持Vim/Neovim集成表示欢迎，认为这是积极的特性。

• **静态类型语言的接近程度**（liotier）：讨论Pyrefly等工具是否使Python更接近静态类型语言。

• **多语言问题的担忧**（melodyogonna）：对新Python工具多采用Rust编写表示担忧，认为这增加了多语言开发的复杂性，希望Mojo能提供解决方案。

• **Rust重写的动机**（phlakaton）：对Pyre到Pyrefly的Rust重写表示好奇，质疑是否仅因Rust流行而选择它，以及其具体优势。

• **对Facebook的不信任**（globalnode）：对Facebook产品不感兴趣，除非有重大创新如AGI。

• **对Rust重写的调侃**（weekendcode）：对Pyrefly使用Rust重写表示调侃，暗示这是预料之中的。

• **对项目范围的批评**（amelius）：认为Pyrefly试图解决太多问题，可能导致项目过于复杂。

• **与现有工具的整合建议**（kingkongjaffa）：质疑为何不直接贡献于uv、ruff和ty，而是推出新项目。

• **对Django支持的担忧**（aleksanb）：指出新类型检查器往往不支持复杂的真实世界Python代码，特别是Django，希望更多工具像TypeScript一样包容广泛的实际使用情况。

补充讨论：
• 对Pyrefly竞争态势的分析，包括与mypy及其他Rust类型检查器的比较。
• 对工具严格性和实用性的用户反馈，以及SQLite数据流管理方法的可行性讨论。
• 对多语言开发复杂性的担忧，以及对特定框架（如Django）支持的期待。

44013913.article_content:
Today we are announcing an alpha version of
Pyrefly
, an open source Python type checker and IDE extension crafted in
Rust
. Pyrefly is a static type checker that analyzes Python code to ensure type consistency and help you catch errors throughout your codebase before your code runs. It also supports IDE integration and CLI usage to give you flexibility in how you incorporate it into your workflow.
The open source community is the backbone of the Python language. We are eager to collaborate on Pyrefly with the community and improve Python’s type system and the many libraries that we all rely on.
Get started
Ready to dive in?
The official Pyrefly website
has all the details, but to quickly get started:
Install
Pyrefly on the command-line:
pip install pyrefly
.
Migrate your existing type checker configuration to Pyrefly
.
Enhance Your IDE: Download the
Pyrefly extension for VSCode
and enjoy a lightning fast IDE experience from starter projects to monorepos.
Leave feedback for us on
GitHub
.
Why we built Pyrefly
Back in 2017, we embarked on a mission to create a type checker that could handle
Instagram’s massive codebase
of typed Python. This mission led to the birth of the
Pyre
type checker, inspired by the robust designs of
Hack
and
Flow
, and written in OCaml to deliver scalable performance.
Over the years, Pyre served us well, but as the type system evolved and the need for typechecking to drive responsive IDE emerged, it was clear that we needed to take a new approach. We explored alternate solutions and leveraged community tools like
Pyright
for code navigation. But the need for an extensible type checker that can bring code navigation, checking at scale, and exporting types to other services drove us to start over, creating Pyrefly.
The principles behind Pyrefly
Today, we’re excited to unveil Pyrefly, a project
we’ve been developing openly on
GitHub
. We invite you to explore our work and try it out on your own project. While a project like Pyrefly is the sum of thousands of technical choices, a few notable principles we’ve followed are:
Performance
We want to shift checks that used to happen later on CI to happening on every single keystroke. That requires checking code at speed (on large codebases we can check 1.8 million lines of code per second!) and careful thought to incrementality and updates. Pyrefly is implemented in Rust and designed for high performance on codebases of all sizes.
IDE first
We want the IDE and command line to share a consistent view of the world, which means crafting abstractions that capture the differences without incurring unnecessary costs. Designing these abstractions from the beginning is much easier than retrofitting them, which we tried with Pyre.
Inference
Some
Python programs are typed
, but many aren’t. We want users to benefit from types even if they haven’t annotated their code – so automatically infer types for returns and local variables and display them in the IDE. What’s more, in the IDE you can even double click to insert these inferred types if you think that would make the program better.
Open source
Python is open source, and hugely popular. The
Python typing specification
is open source, which made Pyrefly vastly easier to develop. Many of the libraries Meta contributes to are open source,( e.g.,
PyTorch
).
Pyrefly is also open source,
available on GitHub
under the
MIT license
, and we encourage
pull requests
and
issue reports
. We also have a
Discord channel
for more free flowing discussions. We would love to build a community around Pyrefly.
The future of Pyrefly
We will work with the Python community to drive the language forward and improve the developer experience. Since the beginning of Pyre, we open sourced our code and contributed a number of PEPs alongside the community of type checker maintainers. We feel we can do more with Pyrefly to help Python developers leverage the benefits of types for developers, library authors, and folks just learning the language.
Meta has leveraged types in dynamic languages from the beginning and knows the significant benefits it brings to developer productivity and security. We plan to share more of our learnings and tooling with
blogs
, better types in the ecosystem and language enhancements.
Today we’re releasing Pyrefly as an alpha. At the same time, we’re busy burning down the long-tail of bugs and features aiming to remove the alpha label this Summer. Your feedback is invaluable to get there, so please give it a try and
report your bugs
or things you think can be improved. Even if Pyrefly isn’t right for your project, we would love to hear how you use types and what you would like to see improved in your editor.
Join us on the journey as we help illuminate your bugs with Pyrefly. Happy coding! 🐍✨
Hear more about Pyrefly
Check out the
episode of the Meta Tech Podcast
where several team members share their experience developing Pyrefly and technical details for how it works. We also just
talked at PyCon US
about

data.title: How I fixed the infamous Basilisk II Windows “Black Screen” bug in 2013
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者Doug Brown在2013年如何修复了Basilisk II在Windows系统上的“黑屏” bug。Basilisk II是一款68k Mac模拟器，在较新的Windows版本（如Vista和7）上运行时，常出现启动后黑屏无法启动Mac系统的问题，而Windows 2000和XP则较少出现此问题。作者通过添加调试输出追踪代码运行情况，最终发现问题出在视频刷新函数`video_refresh_window_vosf()`中。当视频功能未能正确标记需要更新时，就会出现黑屏。虽然旧版本的Basilisk II（build 142）没有此问题，但缺乏性能改进。作者通过调试解决了这个长期存在的bug，使得模拟器在Windows 7上能够正常运行。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows系统演变及其相关技术变化（如内存分配和安全强化），以及在现代系统上模拟旧系统的体验。

不同观点：
• [RJIb8RBYxzAMX9u] 对文章中提到的在现代虚拟机中调试旧系统（如Windows Vista和7）的过程表示惊叹。他提到自己最早使用的是68k Mac，无法想象如今可以轻松模拟多层系统，感慨现代计算资源的丰富。该评论主要表达对技术进步的感慨和惊讶。

• [MBCook] 认为文章中提到的内存分配变化与Vista引入的地址空间布局随机化（ASLR）技术有关，这是微软在Vista开发期间为了加强安全性所做的改变。他还对最初的内存分配方式表示好奇，希望了解其原因。该评论侧重于技术细节和安全性改进。

• [rcarmo] 提到自己在GNOME环境下运行BasiliskII模拟器时遇到分辨率设置问题，程序多次设置窗口大小失败，最终进入了不符合预期的分辨率模式。尽管进行了手动配置，问题仍然存在。该评论聚焦于现代环境下运行旧软件时遇到的实际技术问题。

• [cardanome] 分享了自己曾在PlayStation Portable上运行BasiliskII的经历，虽然没有具体说明目的，但表示对这个经历感到满意。该评论更偏向于个人体验，展示了在非传统设备上运行模拟器的可行性。

补充讨论：
• 技术进步带来的计算资源丰富性是讨论中的一个亮点，特别是[RJIb8RBYxzAMX9u]对现代计算能力的感慨，反映了技术发展的迅速。
• 安全性改进如ASLR的引入是另一个值得注意的讨论点，[MBCook]特别提到了这一点，并对其技术原理表示关注。
• 实际运行旧软件和模拟器时遇到的技术问题也是讨论的一部分，[rcarmo]的评论展示了在现代系统上运行旧软件时可能遇到的兼容性问题。
• 最后，[cardanome]的评论提供了一个有趣的非传统使用案例，展示了模拟器在不同设备上的广泛适用性。

How I fixed the infamous Basilisk II Windows “Black Screen” bug in 2013
Doug Brown
Bug fixes
,
Windows
2025-05-14
I’ve been noticing a lot of fun stories lately about bugs in old software that suddenly showed up in newer Windows versions. For example,
here’s an excellent writeup by Silent
about a bug in
Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
that laid dormant until Windows 11 24H2 came out.
MattKC also recently posted a cool video
about the massive project of decompiling
LEGO Island
, which also solved the mystery of the “exit glitch” that happened in newer versions of Windows. Nathan Baggs has also been at it again,
fixing a modern compatibility issue
with
Sid Meier’s Alpha Centauri
this time.
I won’t spoil these stories for you, but they all reminded me of a bug that I fixed twelve years ago in
Basilisk II
but never wrote about until now. Basilisk II is one of the more popular 68k Mac emulators, allowing you to run an old Mac system on your modern machine. Nowadays, you can even run it in your browser using
Infinite Mac
! Here’s a screenshot of Basilisk II running on my Windows 10 machine.
The bug was: when you launched it, the emulated Mac would just sit there with a black screen rather than booting up. It didn’t happen every time, which really confused everybody. The problem seemed to be way more common on newer Windows versions, which were Vista and 7 at the time, but people also occasionally saw it on XP too. It definitely failed most of the time for me with Windows 7. Nobody was seeing this issue on Mac OS X or Linux.
To re-familiarize myself with this bug for the purposes of writing this post, I downloaded
the broken version from the Internet Archive
and tried it out in some virtual machines. Windows 2000 and XP ran it without any trouble on the first try, but Vista and 7 didn’t:
Basilisk II has a UI quirk that’s really annoying in this particular situation: the close button doesn’t work. You have to cleanly shut down the emulated machine in order to exit, which is impossible to do when you’re stuck with a black screen. This functionality is useful to protect you from losing data in the emulator when it’s working correctly, but it meant that whenever it started with a black screen, I had to go into the Task Manager, right-click on the process in the list, and choose “End Task”. How irritating! It took me about 10 tries before I was able to convince it to run properly without the black screen. No wonder I had tortured myself with this bug fix back in 2013.
Back in the day, there were all kinds of interesting theories and solutions posted by users about this problem.
One person blamed a Bluetooth-related “BTTray.exe” service
. Someone else found that
opening the hard disk image with HFVExplorer before running Basilisk
would allow it to work. Another person observed that
running it as Administrator
fixed the issue.
Compatibility Mode settings
were also a common workaround.
Somebody was even using Safe Mode
to get around it. People had been complaining about this
as far back as 2005
. Given that there were so many differing explanations with varying success, it seemed likely that none of them could truly be the answer.
The only solution that worked for everyone was to revert to an outdated version of Basilisk II from 2001, known as “build 142”. This was sometimes referred to as the pre-JIT version, because it came out before a just-in-time compiler was added to the 68k emulation to drastically improve performance. The old version worked fine, but it lacked all of the modern (at the time) improvements such as JIT.
Anyway, in 2013 I was also affected by this problem on my Windows 7 computer, and decided to take a stab at fixing it. This bug extermination tale isn’t quite as epic as the three linked above, because Basilisk II is open-source. I had access to all the code to see what was going on. But still, even having the source code, I had no idea where to start looking. Why would the behavior randomly change between runs? Maybe an uninitialized variable? Why were modern Windows versions more likely to cause it to fail?
Since I was able to reproduce both a failure case and a success case, I added a bunch of debug trace output to Basilisk II. I wanted to see what was changing between a successful run and an unsuccessful run. I focused on the video code. Was video actually working internally and failing to be displayed in the window, or was something deeper screwing up the video and/or causing the emulated machine to fail to boot?
This iterative testing and debug tracing process revealed that
redraw_func()
in BasiliskII/src/SDL/video_sdl.cpp was periodically called during both failures and successes, but the display was only ever found to be “dirty” and needing an update in
video_refresh_window_vosf()
when video worked correctly. When the black screen bug was happening, the

data.title: Proton threatens to quit Switzerland over new surveillance law
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: 瑞士正考虑修改监控法，要求VPN和消息应用程序识别并保留用户数据。Proton公司（提供VPN和加密邮件服务）的CEO安迪·严（Andy Yen）表示，若该法律通过，Proton将被迫改变其加密方式和无日志政策，可能不得不迁离瑞士。他认为这将严重侵犯隐私权，并损害瑞士的国际竞争力。另一家瑞士公司NymVPN也表示，若新规实施，将同样选择离开。目前，相关公众咨询已结束，瑞士政府尚未做出最终决定。严强调，希望瑞士能制定更合理的法律，让Proton能在国内外保持竞争力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：瑞士法律修订对Proton等隐私保护服务的影响及潜在后果

不同观点：
• sschueller：认为该法律修改在早期阶段就已经失败，并且遭到各方反对，没有通过的可能性。
• Aeyxen：强调Proton不仅仅是营销“瑞士隐私”，而是在技术上实现了无保留（无日志、无追踪）。如果瑞士法律改变，Proton应该离开并重新部署到法律与技术现实相符的地方，否则只是形式上的安全。
• nottorp：提到Techradar网站的用户体验问题，暗示对媒体内容质量的不满，但未直接讨论法律修改的影响。
• ncr100：质疑该法律修改背后的推动者，并试图理解Threema和Proton在此事上的立场，不确定是政府中的某个实体还是团体试图掌控信息。
• Tika2234：表示会根据Proton CEO的承诺采取行动，若Proton不离开瑞士将终止其付费账户，并抵制瑞士的其他在线服务。
• crossroadsguy：质疑Proton离开瑞士后还能以什么作为独特卖点，调侃是否会用“前瑞士隐私”作为宣传。
• OutOfHere：指出Proton若离开瑞士，没有太多其他合适的国家可选，欧盟国家同样受欧盟法规限制，可能只能去像塞舌尔或巴拿马等地，但服务器仍需放在其他地方。
• croemer：仅对标题的语法提出修改建议，未深入讨论内容。
• tempodox：引用“对隐私权的重大侵犯”并质疑恐惧和权威主义是否成功影响了政策的制定，暗示对瑞士自身利益的损害。
• pmkary：简单指出“瑞士隐私”将不复存在。
• juancroldan：批评推动该法律修改的政客为数字文盲，暗示对政策制定者能力的质疑。
• piuantiderp：认为整个事件是场“表演”，暗示对讨论的实际效果持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于瑞士法律修订是否会实质性影响Proton等隐私保护服务的运营，以及这些公司是否应采取行动（如撤离瑞士）来保护用户隐私。
• Proton的“瑞士隐私”品牌形象受到关注，若法律通过，其市场定位和独特卖点可能受到影响。
• 讨论中还涉及对政客和技术理解的批评，以及对隐私保护技术与法律环境之间矛盾的担忧。
• 关于Proton若离开瑞士后可能的去向和实际影响，用户意见不一，有的认为没有更好的选择，有的则认为瑞士作为安全港的地位将丧失。

44014808.article_content:
(Image credit: Photo by FABRICE COFFRINI/AFP via Getty Images)
Proton CEO confirmed the company will leave Switzerland if new controversial surveillance rules pass
An amendment to the current surveillance law would require VPNs and messaging apps to identify and retain user data
Another Swiss company, NymVPN, is also ready to leave the country instead of undermining its privacy and security infrastructure
Proton confirms the company will leave Switzerland if new controversial surveillance rules pass.
Switzerland is
considering amending its surveillance law
, with experts warning against the risk to secure encryption and online anonymity in the country. Specifically, the amendment could require all VPN services, messaging apps, and social networks to identify and retain user data – an obligation that is now limited to mobile networks and internet service providers.
The firm behind one of the
best VPN
and encrypted email services, Proton, is ready to fight back on behalf of the privacy of its over 100 million users. Other Swiss-based companies, like
NymVPN
, are also doing the same.
You may like
"Weakening encryption would make European security worse" – the VPN industry reacts to the EU's plan for end-to-end encryption backdoors
VPN services may soon become a new target of EU lawmakers after being deemed a "key challenge"
"A dangerous approach" – Experts urge the Swedish Parliament to reject the encryption backdoor law
TechRadar needs you!
We want to know what you think about the world of VPNs. Whether you're a novice or a VPN pro, we want to hear your thoughts. Don't worry, though, your responses are completely anonymous, and it takes less than five minutes to complete!
To take part, click the link below:
https://futurenet.questionpro.eu/tr-vpn
No choice but to leave
In an
interview with RTS
(Radio Télévision Suisse) on May 13, 2025, Proton CEO Andy Yen slammed the proposed amendment as a "major violation of the right to privacy" that will also harm the country's reputation and its ability to compete on an international level.
"This revision attempts to implement something that has been deemed illegal in the EU and the United States. The only country in Europe with a roughly equivalent law is Russia," said Yen.
The amendment
aims to expand the number of service providers targeted to include so-called "derived service providers". Crucially, the new provisions will introduce three new types of information and two types of monitoring.
If the changes pass, Proton will be forced to modify how
Proton Mail
and
Proton VPN
handle encryption, alongside its strict no-log policies – something the company isn't willing to do.
"I think we would have no choice but to leave Switzerland," said Yen. "The law would become almost identical to the one in force today in Russia. It's an untenable situation. We would be less confidential as a company in Switzerland than Google, based in the United States. So it's impossible for our business model."
In Switzerland, the new version of the surveillance law aims to make it impossible for Proton, Threema and@nymproject to operate from Switzerland. We are in the consultation phase. We will fight. https://t.co/BcMBxzIPFC
March 25, 2025
Proton is not alone in feeling this way, though.
A new player in the VPN world,
NymVPN
has also been publicly fighting Swiss government plans since the beginning.
Talking to TechRadar, Nym's co-founder and COO, Alexis Roussel, confirmed that Nym will do the same and leave Switzerland if the new surveillance rules are enforced.
What's next?
As public consultations ended on May 6, 2025, we will now have to wait and see what the Swiss government decides.
Nonetheless, Roussel confirmed to TechRadar that there has been significant push-back from political parties and Swiss companies.
Some Cantons,
including Geneva
, have even called on the right to digital integrity as an argument against these rules. Roussel was the main originator of the initiative that
introduced this new right
to protect citizens' online privacy and data – in Geneva in 2023 and Neuchâtel in 2024 – with over 90% consensus.
Yen also told RTS to be more optimistic, despite pointing out how this matter shows the need for a more balanced approach when it comes to crafting new laws.
"If we can get Bern to adopt common-sense rules that allow companies like Proton to be competitive in Switzerland and around the world, I will stay, take my passport, and continue to invest in Switzerland," he added.
You might also like
Windscribe CEO speaks out against global threats to no-log VPNs
Encryption backdoors: privacy can be misused, "but the cost of a world without is so much higher"
"A win for privacy" – Florida rejects the encryption backdoor law for social media
Chiara Castro
News Editor (Tech Software)
Chiara is a multimedia journalist committed to covering stories to help promote the rights and denounce the abuses of the digital side of life – wherever cybersecurity, markets, and politics tangle up. S

data.title: O2 VoLTE: locating any customer with a phone call
data.author: kragniz
data.article_summary: 本文揭示了O2英国的VoLTE服务存在安全漏洞，导致用户位置信息在未经其知晓的情况下暴露给通话发起者。作者通过使用Network Signal Guru应用分析IMS信令消息，发现O2的IMS服务器在通话过程中传输了包含用户IMSI、IMEI和Cell ID的详细信息。这些信息可用于通过公开工具（如cellmapper.net）定位用户的大致地理位置。具体而言，通话发起者可以获取接收方的网络信息、位置区域代码和小区ID，从而推断其位置。这一漏洞严重威胁用户隐私，显示了复杂网络服务配置不当可能引发的安全风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：O2网络中的隐私和安全问题，以及相关技术和法律争议

不同观点：
• lol768指出，通过邮件向O2报告问题后未收到任何回复，质疑O2的响应速度和安全措施。同时对Virgin Media地址的使用提出疑问，并建议国家网络安全中心（NCSC）可能更适合处理此类问题。
• edent提到O2曾有一个负责任的披露地址，但几年前被移除。他回忆过去O2的安全团队很优秀，但近年来团队似乎已经解散。
• Aeyxen认为这不是一个理论上的漏洞，而是由于懒惰的实施所致，其他英国网络已经解决了这个问题。他引用了相关研究论文，指出该问题自LTE推出以来就存在。
• andix指出，该问题在大多数司法管辖区可能不会被视为黑客行为，因为数据是由网络自愿发送的，并没有系统被欺骗。他强调了意图非法访问数据与被动接收数据的区别。
• kjellsbells对呼叫发起者如何看到SIP消息表示好奇，并质疑是否因为OP在设备上运行分析所致。
• jonathantf2批评O2的服务质量，认为他们是最差的网络，仅因为某些特权（如Priority门票）才保留O2 SIM卡。
• ajb提到giffgaff也使用O2网络但声称未受影响，怀疑这是因为giffgaff有自己的服务实现，但同时对giffgaff和O2的合并表示担忧。
• celsoazevedo认为这是一个严重问题，指出O2是英国最大的移动网络，并与政府有合同。他对O2的内部混乱和系统过时提出批评。
• cloudref建议通过关闭VoLTE来缓解此问题，但发现新版iPhone没有该选项。
• edude03假设必须保持足够长的通话时间才能发送调试头，建议通过不接听未知号码来缓解问题。
• ivanvanderbyl对新西兰的O2是否存在相同问题表示好奇，并提到他因O2的免费漫游和VoLTE通话而转网。
• usr1106认为根据GDPR，这种行为显然是违法的，质疑英国脱欧后是否仍适用类似原则。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的技术问题包括VoLTE、SIP消息的可见性、GRE隧道加密等。
• 法律问题主要围绕GDPR和数据隐私，特别是英国脱欧后的法律适用性。
• 对O2内部管理和安全团队效率的批评也是一个重要讨论点。

44014046.article_content:
O2 VoLTE: locating any customer with a phone call
Privacy is dead: For multiple months, any O2 customer has had their location exposed to call initiators without their knowledge.
~
6
min
s
to read
Published
17 May 2025 13:30
This is a guest article written by
Daniel Williams
.
Introduction
Voice over LTE (VoLTE) is a way to make calls via an internet-based protocol on mobile networks using a standard called IP Multimedia Subsystem
(IMS). IMS implementations have historically caused trouble due to their increased complexity and device interdependence. This increase in
complexity has traditionally only externally manifested with device incompatibility problems. In the past, it wasn't uncommon to find devices
that required special firmware to utilise VoLTE and WiFi Calling.
However, I have always been interested in another risk to this increased complexity.
Security.
With an IMS implementation, it is up to the mobile network to choose how they want to implement the services, and what configurations they want
to use. Your phone then talks directly with these servers. Mobile networks have a responsibility to ensure that these servers are kept up to date
and secure, and that their configurations do not lead to unnecessary data exposure.
Unfortunately, today we will be looking at a great example of a mobile network that has validated my concerns.
O2 UK
On 27 March 2017, O2 UK launched their first IMS service.
[1]
Dubbed "4G Calling" by the network, it
provided improved voice quality and a better in-call data experience as customers did not drop down to 3G when making a call.
As someone who had recently moved to O2, I was interested in the network's IMS implementation, particularly which voice codecs were supported by
the network for calls made on 4G/WiFi Calling.
Using an application known as Network Signal Guru (NSG) on my rooted Google Pixel 8, I called another O2 customer (with a 4G VoLTE compatible
device) to try and determine audio quality.
A bug within NSG on modern Google Pixel devices with Samsung Modems means that the VoLTE section of the the app doesn't automatically populate
the codec used for the current call, meaning that I instead had to look at the raw IMS signalling messages sent between my device and the network
to find this out.
Signalling messages
Quite quickly I realised something was wrong. The responses I got from the network were extremely detailed and long, and were unlike anything I
had seen before on other networks. The messages contained information such as the IMS/SIP server used by O2
(
Mavenir UAG
) along with version numbers, occasional error messages raised by the
C++ services processing the call information when something went wrong, and other debugging information. However, most notable were a set of five
headers near the bottom of the message:
SIP Msg
...
P-Mav-Extension-IMSI: 23410123456789
P-Mav-Extension-IMSI: 23410987654321
P-Mav-Extension-IMEI: 350266809828927
P-Mav-Extension-IMEI: 350266806365261
...
Cellular-Network-Info: 3GPP-E-UTRAN-FDD;utran-cell-id-3gpp=2341010037A60773;cell-info-age=26371
Synthesised excerpt of IMS signalling message for demonstration; not a genuine IMEI/IMSI/cell ID.
Two sets of IMSIs, two sets of IMEIs, and a Cell ID header. How curious…
Sure enough, when comparing both the IMSIs and IMEIs in the message to those of my own devices, I had been given both the IMSI and IMEI of my
phone which initiated the call,
but also the call recipient's
.
Curious, I looked into the
Cellular-Network-Info
header. I had never seen this SIP header before but a quick bit of research led me to learn
how to decode it. The start of the value,
3GPP-E-UTRAN-FDD
indicates that the cell data is for 4G (officially known as E-UTRAN) FDD (frequency
division duplex). The folllowing section starting with
utran-cell-id-3gpp
is broken down into 3 parts:
the first 5–6 digits are the network PLMN
of the recipient
the following 4 characters are the
recipient's
Location Area Code (LAC) in hexadecimal
the final 7 characters are the
recipient's
Cell ID, again in hexadecimal
The final section represents how old the data is in seconds. This is present when the device isn't currently connected to a network, such as when
you have no signal or are relying on WiFi Calling.
That means for the above example, we are able to work out that the recipient:
is currently connected to the O2 network (234-10)
is within LAC 0x1003 (decimal: 4009) on Cell ID 0x7a60773 (decimal: 128321395)
uses a Google Pixel 9 (IMEI: 350266806365261)
has an O2 SIM (IMSI: 23410987654321)
This is bad.
With all this information, we can make use of publicly crowdsourced data, collected by tools such as
cellmapper.net
, to
cross-reference this information to work out a general location of the user.
First, we just throw the Cell ID into a tool that calculates what site ID this corresponds to:
Cellmapper's cell ID calculator
Then we just have to search for that site on Cellmapper's map:
O2 UK eNB 501255 on Cellmapper
Here, you can

• 讨论中涉及的技术问题包括VoLTE、SIP消息的可见性、GRE隧道加密等。
• 法律问题主要围绕GDPR和数据隐私，特别是英国脱欧后的法律适用性。
• 对O2内部管理和安全团队效率的批评也是一个重要讨论点。

data.title: Espanso – Cross-Platform Text Expander Written in Rust
data.author: kartikarti
data.article_summary: Espanso 是一个跨平台的文本扩展工具，使用 Rust 编写，支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux。它可以自动检测特定关键字并替换为预设内容，帮助用户节省打字时间、创建代码片段、执行自定义脚本、使用表情符号等。Espanso 支持图片、Emoji、日期扩展、正则触发器、应用特定配置，并具有内置的包管理器和基于文件的配置系统。此外，它还提供实验性的 Wayland 支持。用户可以通过官方文档、Subreddit 或 Discord 获取帮助和参与社区。Espanso 是免费开源的，遵循 GPL-3.0 许可。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Espanso及其他类似工具的功能、优缺点、以及使用体验

不同观点：
• BarryGuff认为AlomWare Toolbox更适合他，因为它不仅支持热键触发，还能通过PC通知中的文本内容触发输入。
• n8henrie赞赏Espanso的跨平台支持，并提到其开源社区的友好和贡献者受到尊重，这使他感到受欢迎。
• majkinetor则更偏向于Autohotkey，尤其是在Windows上，因为其hotstrings功能更强大，且可以通过Wine在Linux上使用。
• behnamoh曾经使用Espanso，但因一些bug和其他工具（如Raycast、BetterTouchTool）的类似功能而转用它们。然而，由于Raycast的AI功能不符合其需求，他计划重回Espanso的怀抱。
• henriquemaia分享了在Linux上使用Espanso的长期经验，强调其易于安装和维护，并且在特定场景下（如在线会议）非常有用。

补充讨论：
• tathagatadg关注如何设计触发器以减少认知负担，并提出了命名空间和冲突避免的策略，同时考虑利用chatgpt生成触发器。
• Wolfbeta提到Espanso也有Android版本，提供了扩展到移动设备的解决方案。
• lamg认为Espanso解决的问题应该由GUI工具包（如GTK、QT）来解决，而不是依赖于类似键盘记录器的工具。

• 不同用户对Espanso和其他工具（如AlomWare Toolbox、Autohotkey、Raycast）的功能和使用体验有不同偏好。

data.title: FreeBASIC is a free/open source BASIC compiler for Windows DOS and Linux
data.author: 90s_dev
data.article_summary: FreeBASIC是一个免费、开源的BASIC编译器，支持Windows、DOS和Linux系统。它具有高兼容性、强大且富有表现力，可在"QB"模式下无缝运行多数QuickBASIC程序。其默认模式下则需对程序进行调整。FreeBASIC使用GNU工具作为后端，支持C和部分C++库，并具备C风格预处理器功能。它可以创建控制台和图形界面程序，速度接近GCC等主流工具。该项目包含跨平台开发工具，支持多种架构和第三方库绑定，如Allegro、SDL、OpenGL等。FreeBASIC不仅兼容QuickBASIC语法，还扩展了更多数据类型和现代编程特性，适用于多种编程范式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源微软旧工具的讨论，特别是与BASIC和MASM等工具相关的话题，以及这些工具在现代系统中的可用性。

不同观点：
• Firehawke认为微软应该开源更多旧工具，如MASM、QuickBasic和DOS版的VisualBasic。他认为这些工具对学习和研究有价值，并且由于这些工具已经过时，开源不会对微软造成经济损失。

• Anta40提到自己拥有2000年代电脑杂志附带的CD，其中包含90年代的代码档案，并指出FBC可以编译许多这些代码。不过，提到仍然缺乏macOS支持。

• Gus_massa提供了一个旧讨论的链接，表明该话题之前已被讨论过，并引导读者查看该讨论。

• Orionblastar分享了几个可以运行旧BASIC程序的现代模拟器和编译器，如PC-BASIC和FreeBASIC，提供了实际的工具供参考。

• Larodi质疑微软为何不支持BASIC遗产，认为即便没有微软的支持，BASIC遗产仍然存在。

• Andrea76提出一个实际需求，询问是否存在带有表单设计器的IDE，类似于Visual Basic。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的工具包括MASM、QuickBasic、VisualBasic（DOS版）、GW-BASIC、PC-BASIC和FreeBASIC。
• 强调了旧工具在现代系统中的兼容性问题，例如macOS支持的缺乏。
• 提出了对微软支持BASIC遗产的质疑和实际需求，如IDE表单设计器的需求。

争议焦点：微软是否应该开源其旧工具以及如何在现代系统中有效使用这些工具。

FreeBASIC is a self-hosting compiler which makes use of the GNU binutils programming tools as
backends and can produce console, graphical/GUI executables, dynamic and static libraries.
FreeBASIC fully supports the use of C libraries and has partial C++ library support. This lets
programmers use and create libraries for C and many other languages. It supports a C style
preprocessor, capable of multiline macros, conditional compiling and file inclusion.
FreeBASIC has been rated close in speed with mainstream tools, such as GCC.
Get FreeBASIC
More about FreeBASIC
The FreeBASIC project is a set of cross-platform development tools, consisting of a compiler,
GNU-based assembler, linker and archiver, and supporting runtime libraries, including a software-based
graphics library. The compiler, fbc, currently supports building for i386-based architectures on the DOS,
Linux, Windows and Xbox platforms. The project also contains thin bindings (header files) to some popular
3rd party libraries such as the C runtime library, Allegro, SDL, OpenGL, GTK+, the Windows API and many
others, as well as example programs for many of these libraries.
FreeBASIC is a high-level programming language supporting procedural, object-orientated and
meta-programming paradigms, with a syntax compatible to Microsoft QuickBASIC. In fact, the
FreeBASIC project originally began as an attempt to create a code-compatible, free alternative
to Microsoft QuickBASIC, but it has since grown into a powerful development tool. FreeBASIC
can be seen to extend the capabilities of Microsoft QuickBASIC in a number of ways, supporting
more data types, language constructs, programming styles, and modern platforms and APIs.
Any type of program can be written with FreeBASIC, see our
Gallery of Applications
for some notable examples.

data.title: Understanding Transformers via N-gram Statistics
data.author: pona-a
data.article_summary: 本文通过N-gram统计方法来理解基于Transformer的大语言模型（LLM）的工作机制。作者研究了简单N-gram规则对Transformer预测的近似程度，提出了几种新发现：无需保留集检测过拟合的方法、量化Transformer从简单到复杂规则的学习进程、以及规则复杂性增加时Transformer预测的近似程度。实验表明，在TinyStories和Wikipedia数据集上，分别有79%和68%的Transformer下一词预测与N-gram规则一致。研究成果有助于揭示Transformer的内在工作原理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一篇被NeurIPS 2024接收的论文及其相关技术方法的讨论，包括对LLM（大语言模型）与简单模型（如N-gram）之间关系的分析，以及对论文发表和研究工作的看法。

不同观点：
• cschmidt认为这篇论文不仅仅是预印本，已经被NeurIPS 2024接收为海报展示，并且相关数据和演示资料都已经公开。这表明该研究具有一定的正式性和可验证性。
• bilsbie提出一个有趣的想法，是否可以用复杂的马尔科夫链替代Transformer模型，并建议通过一种元链机制来实现类似注意力的功能。
• montebicyclelo引用论文中的数据，指出LLM在简单数据集上的预测结果与N-gram模型的规则有较高的吻合度（如TinyStories和Wikipedia数据集上分别为79%和68%），但同时也强调剩余部分的困难是简单模型无法处理而Transformer表现优异的地方。
• pona-a则进一步思考，是否可以通过增加置信度度量来使N-gram模型作为快速推测解码器，但也担心大量显式规则可能会导致实际应用中的不切实际。

补充讨论：
• maz1b对讨论的热度与参与度表示不解，认为既然LLM基于人类输入和努力，是否可以通过重新发布针对不同LLM的论文来持续产出研究成果。
• justanotherjoe对将LLM简化为N-gram模型的观点表示反对，认为这是倒退且缺乏学术深度，并指出作者在一个月内提交了10篇论文，质疑这种高产是否正常。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于LLM是否可以通过简单的N-gram模型部分替代，以及这种观点是否低估了LLM的复杂性和能力。

Title:
Understanding Transformers via N-gram Statistics
Authors:
Timothy Nguyen
View a PDF of the paper titled Understanding Transformers via N-gram Statistics, by Timothy Nguyen
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Transformer based large-language models (LLMs) display extreme proficiency with language yet a precise understanding of how they work remains elusive. One way of demystifying transformer predictions would be to describe how they depend on their context in terms of simple template functions. This paper takes a first step in this direction by considering families of functions (i.e. rules) formed out of simple N-gram based statistics of the training data. By studying how well these rulesets approximate transformer predictions, we obtain a variety of novel discoveries: a simple method to detect overfitting during training without using a holdout set, a quantitative measure of how transformers progress from learning simple to more complex statistical rules over the course of training, a model-variance criterion governing when transformer predictions tend to be described by N-gram rules, and insights into how well transformers can be approximated by N-gram rulesets in the limit where these rulesets become increasingly complex. In this latter direction, we find that for 79% and 68% of LLM next-token distributions on TinyStories and Wikipedia, respectively, their top-1 predictions agree with those provided by our N-gram rulesets.

44016564.article_summary: 本文通过N-gram统计方法来理解基于Transformer的大语言模型（LLM）的工作机制。作者研究了简单N-gram规则对Transformer预测的近似程度，提出了几种新发现：无需保留集检测过拟合的方法、量化Transformer从简单到复杂规则的学习进程、以及规则复杂性增加时Transformer预测的近似程度。实验表明，在TinyStories和Wikipedia数据集上，分别有79%和68%的Transformer下一词预测与N-gram规则一致。研究成果有助于揭示Transformer的内在工作原理。

data.title: Bike-mounted sensor could boost the mapping of safe cycling routes
data.author: yunusabd
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种由华盛顿大学研发的自行车传感器ProxiCycle，旨在提升安全骑行路线的测绘。该设备安装在自行车左把手，利用红外光传感器监测附近车辆，通过蓝牙将数据传至手机应用，记录与汽车的近距离接触。传感器成本不到25美元，每次充电可使用12小时。初步测试显示，ProxiCycle能准确识别危险路段，比现有依赖事故报告或主观评价的测绘方法更客观。研究团队计划在更多城市进行大规模测试，以帮助新手骑行者选择安全路线，促进骑行安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何提高自行车骑行安全及相关技术解决方案

不同观点：
• **文化与政治问题优先**：[danieldk] 认为，尽管技术可以帮助绘制安全路线，骑行安全更多是文化与政治问题。他主张通过建立独立的自行车道、修改法律让汽车司机在事故中承担更多责任、培训司机提高对骑行者的 awareness 等措施来改善骑行安全。

• **技术解决方案的讨论**：[yunusabd] 对传感器技术表示关注，认为该技术能够有效识别大型障碍物（如汽车），并且成本低廉，已经在测试中显示出有效性。该评论提供了具体的技术细节和实现方法。

• **城市设计与基础设施的局限**：[jwagenet] 提到，尽管旧金山有一些保护性自行车道，但大多数骑行路线仍然需要与汽车共享道路，尤其是在住宅区和商业区。这使得完全避免与汽车的接触非常困难。

• **现有商业解决方案**：[s1mon] 指出市场上已经有类似的商业产品，如 Roadio 和 Garmin 的后置雷达与摄像头系统，质疑新发布的产品是否真的具有创新性。

• **骑行者的自我责任**：[kjkjadksj] 认为，骑行者通过占据车道可以提高自身的可见性与安全性，尤其在多车道道路上更为有效。这种观点强调骑行者的主动行为而非依赖基础设施。

• **基础设施优先于技术**：[andrewshadura] 主张，安全的自行车路线应通过建设固有的安全基础设施来实现，如保护性交叉路口和独立的自行车道，认为技术方案是在寻找问题。

补充讨论：
• **创新与幽默建议**：[nikau] 和 [iosguyryan] 分别以幽默的方式提出喷洒刹车液和使用 FLARM 系统（类似于飞机防撞系统）的建议，尽管是玩笑，但引发了对创新解决方案的思考。

• **骑行者的自我监测**：[pedalpete] 提出使用加速计来监测骑行平稳性，从而间接判断与交通的互动情况，认为这是对现有技术的一种补充。

争议焦点：
• **技术方案与基础设施建设的优先性**：一些评论者强调技术解决方案（如传感器和摄像头）的潜力，而另一些评论者则认为基础设施的改善才是根本解决之道。这种对立反映了在解决骑行安全问题时，技术与基础设施孰先孰后的争议。

• **现有解决方案的创新性**：部分评论者质疑新发布的产品是否真正具有创新性，认为市场上已有类似产品，这引发了对技术进步与市场推广的讨论。

View gallery - 3 images
Studies have shown that many people don't commute by bike due mainly to a fear of being hit by cars. A new bike-mounted proximity sensor has been designed to help such folks, by objectively telling them which streets are the safest for cyclists.
When you look up cycling routes on platforms such as Google Maps, the safety
of
those routes is based mainly on the number of bicycle-automobile collisions that have been reported on them.
Unfortunately, this means that a significant number of such accidents have to occur before a route is deemed unsafe. It also doesn't take into account the smaller "fender-bender" collisions that don't get reported.
Mapping platforms additionally base their recommendations on the
perceived
safety of different streets, as self-reported by cyclists. This is a rather subjective approach. After all, it's certainly possible that motorists may actually tend to give cyclists plenty of space on busy roads that are perceived as being dangerous, while passing dangerously close on quieter "safe" streets.
That's where the new ProxiCycle sensor comes in. It's being developed at the University of Washington, by a team led by computer science and engineering doctoral student Joseph Breda.
The device could cost less than US$25 per unit to build using off-the-shelf components
Breda et al./CHI ‘25
The prototype device simply replaces the bike's existing left-side handlebar plug, where it uses two infrared-light-based time-of-flight sensors to monitor the spaces directly beside and immediately behind the bicycle. Whenever an object is detected, the ProxiCycle utilizes a Bluetooth module to transmit the sensor data to an app on the cyclist's smartphone.
That app uses a special algorithm to determine if the detected object
was
an automobile, and
if
it passed less than 1 m (3.3 ft) from the bike. If the reading meets both of those criteria, it is saved as an example of a motorized vehicle that
passed the cyclist too closely
.
The idea is that over a relatively short period of time, readings gathered from multiple ProxiCycle users could be used to paint a realistic picture of just how dangerous various streets actually are.
The current version of the device has a runtime of approximately 12 hours per battery-charge
Breda et al./CHI ‘25
In an initial test of the technology, seven cyclists rode through Seattle with both the device and a GoPro camera mounted on their bike. Close-passing incidents recorded by the ProxiCycle were found to match up with those captured by the camera.
Next, 15 Seattle cyclists used the device while going on a combined total of 240 bike rides over a two-month period. They recorded 2,050 close passes in that time, with the majority of the incidents taking place in locations where higher-than-average numbers of bike-car collisions had already been reported.
The incidents also mostly occurred in areas that cyclists had previously
perceived
as being dangerous. Importantly, however, the sensor data proved to be a more accurate indicator of just how hazardous those places actually were.
Breda and colleagues now plan on conducting larger-scale studies, which will include testing the ProxiCycle in other cities.
"Experienced cyclists have this mental map of which streets are safe and which are unsafe, and I wanted to find a simple way to pass that knowledge down to novice cyclists," he says. "Cycling is really good for your health and for the environment. Getting more people biking more often is how we reap those rewards and increase safety in numbers for cyclists on the roads."
A
paper
on the research was recently presented at the ACM CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems in Yokohama, Japan.

data.title: “Streaming vs. Batch” Is a Wrong Dichotomy, and I Think It's Confusing
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: Gunnar Morling指出，"流式处理（Streaming） vs. 批处理（Batch）"的二分法具有误导性。实际上，许多流式系统也采用批处理来优化性能，如通过批量传输减少连接开销、提升多线程工作效率等。讨论应更关注"拉取（Pull） vs. 推送（Push）"的语义区别：拉取系统定期查询数据源，可能错过更新或删除；推送系统实时接收数据更新，提供完整数据视图。尽管流式系统复杂性较高，但其优势在于实时数据处理能力。尝试过流式处理的人往往会倾向于更多地使用它。此外，拉取和推送可以互补，例如批量回填数据或在低数据量时暂停流式管道以节省成本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：批处理（batch）与流处理（streaming）在数据处理中的优劣对比，以及在不同场景下的适用性。

不同观点：
• **[matjazk]** 认为λ架构（批处理+流处理）需要维护两个数据处理管道，而κ架构（纯流处理）将批处理视为流处理的特例，简化了维护。
• **[fifilura]** 基于实际经验，认为流处理系统复杂且成本高，维护难度大，通常企业并不需要实时数据处理，简单的批处理和SQL查询即可满足需求。
• **[efitz]** 强调批处理和流处理的核心区别在于数据获取方式和处理模式，批处理是周期性的，而流处理是连续的。
• **[kazinator]** 提出“批处理”的对立面是“交互式处理”，并解释了批处理的历史背景和术语来源，认为流处理中使用了聚合而非批处理。
• **[binoct]** 指出不同人对“流处理”和“批处理”有不同的理解和定义，认为这是语义上的争论，缺乏具体性，强调需要统一的术语。
• **[floating-io]** 认为批处理是有限大小的数据组，而流处理是实时传输的无缓冲数据，数据处理方式在接收后无关紧要。
• **[brudgers]** 简单定义流处理数据大小未知且可能是无限的，批处理数据大小已知且有限。
• **[simlevesque]** 质疑一切都是批处理，认为即使是实时流处理也是由批处理组成。
• **[briankelly]** 认为λ架构中的批处理和流处理讨论更多是关于工具和技术的实现，而非单纯的选择问题，两者在延迟和吞吐量上的优化不同。
• **[cgio]** 认为推送批处理系统存在，并坚持流处理和批处理的区别有意义，即使组合使用也不否定其差异。
• **[mannyv]** 认为“推送”和“拉取”比“流处理”和“批处理”更难区分，解释了传统批处理的定义和流处理的实时性。
• **[davery22]** 详细分析了不同场景下快照（pull）和实时视图（push）的需求，强调了两者的互补性和复杂性。
• **[oatmeal_croc]** 简单总结流处理优化延迟，批处理优化效率。
• **[calrain]** 强调批处理由服务器决定资源利用率，可以在服务器有适当资源时进行处理，帮助产品在较低规格的服务器上运行。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于流处理和批处理的定义和适用场景，特别是在复杂系统中的实现和维护成本。
• 不同观点中对于“批处理”和“流处理”的定义和区别的理解存在较大差异，反映了术语使用上的混乱。
• 实际应用中的需求和选择往往不是非此即彼，而是需要根据具体场景权衡选择合适的架构和技术。
• 强调了语义和术语统一的重要性，特别是在技术讨论中，以避免误解和混淆。

43983201.article_content:
Gunnar Morling
Random Musings on All Things Software Engineering
Gunnar Morling
Random Musings on All Things Software Engineering
"Streaming vs. Batch" Is a Wrong Dichotomy, and I Think It's Confusing
Posted at May 14, 2025
Often times, "Stream vs. Batch" is discussed as if it’s one
or
the other, but to me this does not make that much sense really.
Many streaming systems will apply batching too, i.e. processing or transferring multiple records (a "batch") at once,
thus offsetting connection overhead, amortizing the cost of fanning out work to multiple threads,
opening the door for highly efficient SIMD processing, etc., all to ensure high performance.
The prevailing trend towards storage/compute separation in data streaming and processing architectures
(for instance, thinking of platforms such as WarpStream, and
Diskless Kafka
at large)
further accelerates this development.
Typically, this is happening transparently to users, done in an opportunistic way:
handling all of those records (up to some limit) which have arrived in a buffer since the last batch.
This makes for a very nice self-regulating system.
High arrival rate of records: larger batches, improving throughput.
Low arrival rate: smaller batches, perhaps with even just a single record, ensuring low latency.
Columnar in-memory data formats like
Apache Arrow
are of great help for implementing such a design.
In contrast, what the "Stream vs. Batch" discussion in my opinion should actually be about,
are "Pull vs. Push" semantics:
will the system query its sources for new records in a fixed interval,
or will new records be pushed to the system as soon as possible?
Now, no matter how often you pull,
you can’t convert a pull-based solution into a streaming one.
Unless a source represents a consumable stream of changes itself (you see where this is going),
a pull system may miss updates happening between fetch attempts, as well as deletes.
This is what makes streaming so interesting and powerful:
it provides you with a complete view of your data in real-time.
A streaming system lets you put your data to the
location
where you need it,
in the
format
you need it, and in the
shape
you need it (think denormalization),
immediately as it gets produced or updated.
The price for this is a potentially higher complexity,
for example when reasoning about streaming joins (and their state),
or handling out-of-order data.
But the streaming community is working continuously to improve things here,
e.g. via disaggregated state backends,
transactional stream processing, and much more.
I’m really excited about all the innovation happening in this space right now.
Now, you might wonder: "Do I really need streaming
(push)
, though? I’m fine with batch
(pull)
."
That’s a common and fair question.
In my experience, it is best answered by giving it a try yourself.
Again and again I have seen how folks who were skeptical at first,
very quickly wanted to get real-time streaming for more and more,
if not all of their use cases,
once they had seen it in action once.
If you’ve experienced a data freshness of a second or two in your data warehouse,
you don’t want to ever miss this magic again.
All that being said,
it’s actually not even about pull
or
push so much—​the approaches complement each other.
For instance, backfills often are done via batching, i.e. querying, in an otherwise streaming-based system.
Also, if you want the completeness of streaming but don’t require a super low latency,
you may decide to suspend your streaming pipelines (thus saving cost) in times of low data volume,
resume when there’s new data to process, and halt again.
Batch streaming, if you will.
43983201.article_summary: Gunnar Morling指出，"流式处理（Streaming） vs. 批处理（Batch）"的二分法具有误导性。实际上，许多流式系统也采用批处理来优化性能，如通过批量传输减少连接开销、提升多线程工作效率等。讨论应更关注"拉取（Pull） vs. 推送（Push）"的语义区别：拉取系统定期查询数据源，可能错过更新或删除；推送系统实时接收数据更新，提供完整数据视图。尽管流式系统复杂性较高，但其优势在于实时数据处理能力。尝试过流式处理的人往往会倾向于更多地使用它。此外，拉取和推送可以互补，例如批量回填数据或在低数据量时暂停流式管道以节省成本。

data.title: Xata: Postgres at scale, with copy-on-write branching and anonymization
data.author: mebcitto
data.article_summary: Xata推出了全新的PostgreSQL平台，主打"大规模Postgres"功能，包括即时写时复制（Copy-on-Write）数据分支、数据匿名化、存储与计算分离等特性。该平台适用于需要处理大规模数据和组织挑战的团队，支持零停机进行模式变更和主版本升级，并提供不含个人敏感信息（PII）的开发环境。通过结合开源项目pgstream（支持数据复制和匿名化）和pgroll（零停机模式变更），Xata实现了安全一致的开发工作流。该平台可与现有PostgreSQL服务（如AWS RDS、GCP CloudSQL等）无缝集成，支持在用户自己的云账户中部署，确保数据安全和合规。此外，Xata的存储与计算分离架构允许独立扩展，并按使用量付费，具有高耐用性和自动无限扩展的存储能力。虽然可以在不改变生产数据库的情况下使用Xata，但将生产环境迁移至Xata还能带来成本节约和性能提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Postgres在Kubernetes上的部署与管理、Xata平台的使用体验与定价、技术工具的选择与信任问题

不同观点：
• **关于Postgres在Kubernetes上的"脑裂"问题**：
  - samokhvalov提到他们在Kubernetes上通过CloudNativePG operator部署Postgres实例，并关注是否会出现"脑裂"（split brain）情况，尤其是在大规模部署场景下。这表明了对高可用性及故障处理的担忧。
  
• **Xata平台的功能与定价争议**：
  - joshstrange询问Xata是否允许多个项目或数据库共享同一计算资源，并对Xata过去的复杂定价提出批评，尽管新的定价更易理解。他还提到自己并不需要"大规模"运行Postgres，因此可能只适合使用Xata Lite版本。
  - joshstrange进一步补充，虽然不喜欢被归类为"vibe coded app"用户，但Xata Lite的定价依然难以预估。

• **对Xata平台性能的负面体验**：
  - beeman通过其 mentee 的经验分享，指出Xata与Prisma一起使用时出现了内存不足错误，并且需要额外的"shadow"数据库，而切换到Prisma自己的Postgres托管服务后问题解决。这表明Xata在特定技术栈（如Prisma）中的表现可能不如预期。

• **对开源工具和自建基础设施的信任问题**：
  - paulryanrogers表示尽管看到Xata等工具开源和支持自带云（BYOC）是好事，但由于自己已经解决了类似问题，且没有时间和预算去验证新工具，因此不太会信任这些工具处理复杂Postgres使用场景。
  - gitroom也提到，看到此类工具开源总是让人思考是否值得切换，还是仅仅关乎信任问题。

• **数据库分支（branching）的使用场景讨论**：
  - jatins提出一个更具体的技术问题，询问数据库分支的使用场景，但没有进一步展开讨论。

- 评论中反映了对新工具和平台的信任问题，尤其是在已有自建解决方案的情况下，用户对迁移到新平台的犹豫。
- 对Xata平台定价的批评和复杂性也成为讨论的焦点，尤其对小型项目或不需要大规模运行Postgres的用户来说，如何选择合适的方案成为难题。
- 技术实现中的具体问题（如Prisma与Xata的兼容性）也引发了对平台性能和适用性的质疑。

44016289.article_content:
Xata: Postgres with data branching and PII anonymization
Relaunching Xata as "Postgres at scale". A Postgres platform with Copy-on-Write branching, data masking, and separation of storage from compute.
Author
Tudor Golubenco
Date published
May 14, 2025
Here at Xata, we’ve been quietly busy (re)building a new PostgreSQL platform from scratch. We've incorporated everything we learned from operating a Postgres data platform for over four years, combined with feedback from our customers and our analysis of the gaps in the current market.
The result is an entirely
new Postgres service
that:
Has instant Copy-on-Write branches with data.
Includes data anonymization so that developer branches don’t accidentally contain PII.
Is cloud-agnostic, installable in your own AWS/GCP/Azure account, or even on-prem.
Separates storage from compute with a distributed storage system accessed over NVMe/TCP.
Offers a performance/cost ratio that is very competitive at scale.
We'll dive into the technical details shortly, but let's first talk about who this Postgres platform is for.
Postgres at scale
Our goal is to address the challenges teams face when using Postgres at scale. When we say "scale", we don't only mean technical dimensions like data volume, number of CPUs, GB of RAM, or vertical/horizontal scaling capabilities. While these are included in our definition of "at scale", we also mean organizational challenges such as:
Zero-downtime requirements
when applying schema changes or major version upgrades.
Testing database changes or training AI models on
realistic data sets
that resemble the production data, but without any PII or sensitive data in them.
Fast, cost-efficient
ephemeral environments for developers.
Security and compliance
for companies that deal with sensitive data.
Let’s start by looking at
staging and dev
use cases, and then we’ll be talking about
prod
use cases as well.
Staging and dev use cases
Copy-on-Write branches are a great way to quickly spin up preview or development environments with production data, even when dealing with very large datasets. But on their own, they come with two major limitations:
By design, the branches contain exactly the same data as the parent database,
including private PII/PHI or any other sensitive data
. This often violates compliance requirements and risks exposing data to developers.
When it comes to schema changes, branching-out solves only half of the problem.
The other half is merging back in
. Copy-on-Write branches don't provide a mechanism to safely apply the changes you tested in a branch back to your production environment.
Fortunately, we've been working on these exact problems for quite some time now, through two open-source projects:
pgstream
- PostgreSQL replication with DDL changes, now also with masking/anonymization.
pgroll
- Zero-downtime, reversible, schema changes for PostgreSQL.
The new Xata platform combines these projects with Copy-on-Write branches, creating a complete, safe, and consistent developer workflow for PostgreSQL.
The best part is that
you can use Xata even if you are not looking to change your production Postgres service
. Xata works with and improves your existing PostgreSQL service, whether it's AWS RDS, Amazon Aurora, GCP CloudSQL, Azure Database, or even self-hosted Postgres.
At a high level, adopting Xata looks something like this:
Your production database stays exactly as it is, no changes necessary.
We create a “staging replica” on the Xata platform.
xata clone
, powered by
pgstream
, copies and anonymizes the data on the fly.
xata branch create
lets you to create instant dev branches from the staging replica. These branches contain realistic, anonymized versions of your production data.
Optionally, use
xata roll
, powered by
pgroll
, to test schema changes and safely apply them with zero-downtime to production.
If you don't want to send any data out of your production environment, even if anonymized, you don't have to: we have a
BYOC
(Bring Your Own Cloud) deployment model where all staging and dev branches run in your AWS/GCP/Azure/other account or even on-prem. More about that later.
Prod use cases
While you can get the Xata benefits without running your production on our platform, doing so gives you cost savings, better performance, and other wins in terms of flexibility, extensions, and support.
Xata uses an architecture that
separates storage from compute.
This brings benefits like:
Scaling compute and storage separately.
Storage has its own redundancy, increasing durability.
Pay only for what you use in terms of storage, without needing to overprovision.
Storage simply grows automatically and unbounded, without the risk of running out of disk space.
While services like Amazon Aurora and Neon also separate storage from compute, the Xata implementation is different because it is done strictly at the storage layer. This means that we didn’t have to modify Postgres at all. We simply run vanilla Postgres, and therefore have
100% P

data.title: Experts have it easy (2024)
data.author: veqq
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了专家相比新手在工作效率和成果上的显著差异，并指出这种现象未被充分研究。专家由于工作速度更快，通常会收取更高的时间费用，而新手则往往因为缺乏经验而效率低下，陷入自己制造的复杂问题中，导致时间和精力的浪费。文章通过一个迷宫比喻，描述了新手在迷路时如何做出错误决策，使问题变得更复杂，而专家则能迅速找到有效解决方案。新手常专注于无关紧要的细节，而专家则能直击核心问题。文章强调，简单告诉新手“做得更好”并无助于其进步，有效的反馈应帮助他们改善决策过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何促进初级开发人员成长以及专家与初级人员的互动学习

不同观点：
• **支持与初级人员密切互动**：9dev强调与初级开发人员进行无特定目标的交谈，有助于双方共同成长。这种互动让初级人员更自信，并敢于质疑专家的决定，而专家也能反思自己的方法。joenot443也支持这种观点，认为通过非完美但实际可行的解决方案来评估候选人，比单纯考察算法能力更有价值。

• **注重"草根"和自学经验**：joenot443和coderintherye提到，自学和处理实际技术问题的经验（如安装Ubuntu或修理机械设备）对开发人员成长至关重要。这些经验培养了开发人员的“顽强”精神，使他们能够应对各种技术挑战。

• **专注于利基领域**：coderintherye和giorgioz建议，年轻开发人员应深入新兴领域（如LLM），因为这些领域专家少，竞争小，可以迅速积累经验。

• **专家与 novice 的互动方式争议**：
   - **支持非正式互动**：9dev和pards认为非正式的互动，如“水 cooler”式的交流或结对编程，是知识传递的有效方式。
   - **反对依赖非正式互动**：edelbitter反驳，认为不应依赖偶然的互动进行知识传递，正式记录和系统化的知识分享更有效。

44018301.article_content:
Something thatâs painfully understudied is how experts are more efficient
than novices while achieving better results. I say understudied and not
unstudied, because itâs common knowledge that charging people for their time
results in experts being paid less since they work faster, which is why experts
charge more for their time.
This effect is understudied in the impact it has on novices entering a field. A
Novice will start out being woefully inefficient, putting in incredible amounts
of effort and running through all number of mental hoops in order to maintain
the growing pile of unmaintainable abstractions theyâve developed. An expert
doesnât have to jump through these hoops. They can more clearly see the actual
problem at hand and will more efficiently put their time and effort towards
making progress against the problem. In contrast, novices will spend more time
battling problems they created for themselves. Letâs explore this idea by
looking at two characters entrapped in a maze, and how they go about escaping.
Stuck in a maze: Expert vs Novice
Imagine a world-class navigator being set in a maze. They come well prepared
with compass and paper, and have previously escaped some of the most
dastardly mazes designed by man. Also, imagine yourself. Youâre the Novice in
this scenario. You didnât realise you were being thrown into a maze. You
donât even know if the goal is to get out or to find the centre.
As you go deeper and deeper into the maze, you realise that youâre helplessly
lost. Through a miracle of literary convenience, your expert friend calls you
up and offers advice: âAs soon as you start, keep track of where youâve been
using your ball of twine. Itâll help you keep track of the decisions you makeâ.
You didnât realise the criticality of feline playthings, and so didnât bring
a ball of twine. You also donât remember where you started. You ask your
expert friend for advice on what to do, to which they respond âOh Iâve got no
idea. I never go anywhere without my ball of twine. You just shouldnât have
gotten yourself into this mess in the first place.â
Some of the trickiest tangles Iâve tackled havenât been because the core
problem is difficult, but rather because I was helping someone with less
experience, and they spent several hours getting themselves more and more tied
up. Before asking for help, they made a wrong decision, which maybe solved
their short term problems but shot them in the foot in the long term. This bad
decision made other bad decisions more likely until they were helplessly stuck
in a trap of their own making.
Often this trap is far trickier than anything an expert would let themselves
get into. Novices, on the other hand, can easily make a sequence of bad
decisions that result in an ever increasing cost of solving the problem at
hand. Not only are you lost in the maze without your twine, but you also went
in a mysterious cave that looked kinda interesting at first and now youâre lost
in the dark. Meanwhile, the world-class expert is happily skipping through the
warm sunny parts of the maze, because they knew that the cave would eventually
lead to a dead end.
Iâd like to stress at this point that this is in no way the Noviceâs fault.
They followed the same policy as any expert: âtake best action available to you
at the timeâ. Telling a Novice to âjust be betterâ is not constructive
feedback. This feedback does not lead to them improving over time, since from
the only perspective that matters in this scenario (the Noviceâs), they were
taking the best action available to them. And if youâre giving feedback that
doesnât lead to improvement, whatâs the point of the feedback?
The Novice has a genius idea
Still lost in the maze, you keep walking. Your friend mentioned the ball of
twine, and after thinking for a bit you realise your woollen jumper, if
carefully dismantled, could be a good replacement. Dutifully and with a
concrete objective, you sit down and begin to unravel your jumper. After an
hour or so, youâve got your ball of yarn. After some failed attempts at
unspooling the yarn behind you, you realise one strand of yarn is hopelessly
weak. You decide to braid the yarn, and sit down for another hour to do so.
Itâs pretty boring, but you assume that this is just what solving mazes is
all about.
A bit later, your expert friend calls you up and lambastes you for wasting
time with this yarn business. âIt was clearly never going to workâ he says.
He instructs you to use broken branches from the hedge that makes up
the maze as a way of marking your path. You hadnât realised the maze was made
of hedge until this point.
Novices often spend energy fixing things that are orthogonal to the actual
problem they want to solve, whereas experts are able to better direct their
energy towards the problems they want to solve. This leads to novices having an

44018301.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了专家相比新手在工作效率和成果上的显著差异，并指出这种现象未被充分研究。专家由于工作速度更快，通常会收取更高的时间费用，而新手则往往因为缺乏经验而效率低下，陷入自己制造的复杂问题中，导致时间和精力的浪费。文章通过一个迷宫比喻，描述了新手在迷路时如何做出错误决策，使问题变得更复杂，而专家则能迅速找到有效解决方案。新手常专注于无关紧要的细节，而专家则能直击核心问题。文章强调，简单告诉新手“做得更好”并无助于其进步，有效的反馈应帮助他们改善决策过程。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于信息传播、心理行动（PsyOps）以及网络迷因（meme）在宣传和意识形态中的作用

不同观点：
• **aspenmayer** 提供的链接涉及与心理行动（PsyOps）相关的文档，但没有明确表达个人立场，可能旨在提供背景信息供讨论。
• **findalex** 指出，心理行动（PsyOps）的教义禁止对美国国内受众传递相关信息，直到2012年《国防授权法》（NDAA 2012）之后才有所变化。findalex认为这种教义本质上就是法律，并对法律的演变提供了参考链接。
• **ta988** 简单直接地否定了存在所谓的“反迷因部门”（antimemetics division），暗示可能对讨论内容持怀疑态度或认为其不真实。
• **endoblast** 区分了“宣传”（propaganda）和“迷因”（memeing），认为宣传是推广特定意识形态的工具，而迷因则是自发产生并用以揭示真相。endoblast强调迷因通常是“好”的，因为它们指向现实和真理，而主流宣传则通过选择性使用事实来扭曲真相。
• **webdoodle** 提到自己在Reddit上的账号被封禁，所有帖子和评论被删除，并分享了关于“迷因链”（memetic chaining）的文章链接，似乎对讨论中的主题有专业或深入的兴趣。
• **globalnode** 对讨论内容表达了幽默但略带担忧的态度，认为如果情况不那么危险，会觉得这很有趣，暗示讨论内容可能具有潜在风险。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是心理行动（PsyOps）的合法性和其对国内受众的限制，findalex通过法律文件（NDAA 2012）来支持自己的观点。
• endoblast对迷因和宣传的区分以及对迷因作用的正面评价与其他评论的观点形成对比，尤其是与findalex对PsyOps信息传播的关注形成对照。
• webdoodle的个人经历（账号被封禁）提供了一个关于网络平台内容审核和言论自由的实际案例，增加了讨论的现实维度。
• globalnode的评论则反映了讨论话题的潜在危险性，使得讨论不仅限于理论层面，还涉及实际社会和政治影响。

data.title: ARMv9 Architecture Helps Lift Arm to New Financial Heights
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: Armv9架构的推出带来了更高的授权费和专利费，推动Arm的收入创下新高。在2025财年第四季度，Arm首次突破单季10亿美元收入，全年收入超过40亿美元，其中专利收入首次超过20亿美元。Armv9的专利费高于前代架构，特别是在智能手机和服务器芯片领域增长显著。Arm在云计算和AI部署中愈发成为首选，例如Nvidia的Grace-Blackwell Armv9已全面投产，Google的Axion Armv9已在十个地区部署，微软的Cobalt 100支持多项重要工作负载。AWS在过去两年中超过50%的新CPU容量由Arm架构的Graviton支持。此外，Arm的研发费用占比从53%降至44%，推动营业收入大幅增长。尽管股权投资亏损导致净收入略降，但整体财务表现强劲。Arm的生态系统持续扩展，合作伙伴累计出货已达310亿颗芯片，全球超过2200万开发者为其编写代码。

主要讨论点：ARM架构及其相关技术、市场和政治影响

不同观点：
• [ksec] 认为这篇评论更多是关于ARM新任CEO Rene Haas，而非ARMv9架构本身。他指出，ARM的定价策略一直偏低，即使在提高价格后，其Cortex X系列仍然具有竞争力。他同时希望ARM能在GPU研发上投入更多，并期待Nvidia在Computex 2025上的动态。

• [margorczynski] 提出ARM面临RISC-V和中国CPU的竞争，长期来看可能会因价格劣势失去市场份额。

• [SillyUsername] 关注ARM被出售给Softbank的政治背景，批评英国政府缺乏远见，并对ARM不再属于英国表示不满。他还提到Boris Johnson曾试图让ARM重回伦敦证券交易所（LSE）。

• [Neywiny] 作为ARM微控制器的用户，对v8和M33的进展表示关注，但对M55的推动力不足感到失望。

• [AtlasBarfed] 关心ARM架构对Linux系统效率的影响，并推测未来CPU发展将更专注于AI处理，而不是传统计算效率的提升。他认为ARM、AMD、Intel在追赶Apple的创新上可能会停滞。

• 争议焦点之一是ARM的定价策略及其市场竞争力。
• 政治因素对科技公司所有权的影响，特别是国家安全和经济利益的考量。
• 对未来CPU发展方向的预测，尤其是AI处理和传统计算的优先级变化。
• 不同用户对ARM产品和策略的个人体验和期望差异。

43982495.article_content:
The Armv9 architecture has a lot of technical enhancements to commend it, but as far as Arm Holdings, the creator and licensor of the Arm architecture, is concerned one of the best features of Armv9,
which was first unveiled four years ago
, is that it comes with a higher royalty fee than prior Armv7 and Armv8 architectures.
And that fact, as well as wider adoption of the Arm architecture by hyperscalers and cloud builders for their homegrown CPUs, is lifting Arm to record-breaking revenue heights. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 ended in March, Arm broke through $1 billion in a quarter for the first time, and for all of fiscal 2025, it broke through $4 billion in sales for the first time and royalty revenue broke through $2 billion for the first time. That’s a lot of firsts.
We don’t know how much more expensive Armv9 is compared to Armv8 when it comes to licenses and royalties, but Rene Haas, Arm’s chief executive officer, said on a call with Wall Street analysts that smartphone chip royalties were up 30 percent in the march quarter, compared to only 2 percent growth in shipments of smartphone chips by Arm’s partners. We don’t know that server chips are on the same royalty price curve as smartphone chips, but odds are the delta between architecture versions is similar, and in the case of server CPUs, Arm shipments are also growing fast as the royalties are also higher per unit.
“Arm is now increasingly the first choice for AI cloud deployments,” Haas said on the call. “We expect up to 50 percent of new server chips at hyperscalers to be Arm based this year. Nvidia’s Grace-Blackwell Armv9 is now in full production. Google’s Axion Armv9 now deployed in ten regions, used by 40 of their top 100 customers, offering up to 65 percent better price performance than current generation X86. And Microsoft Cobalt 100 supports major workloads for Databricks, Siemens, Snowflake, and internal services like Teams and Copilot. And over 50 percent of new AWS CPU capacity in the past two years is powered by Arm-based Graviton. We are also seeing strong momentum in custom silicon with companies turning to Arm for CPU, GPU and NPU solutions. This is driving both license and royalty growth.”
In the final quarter of fiscal 2025, Arm posted $607 million in royalty revenues, up 18.1 percent year on year. License and other revenue, including Compute Subsystem (CSS) licensing and IP packages that are now being used by six client device makers, six infrastructure makers, and one car system maker, rose by 53.1 percent to $634 million.
Add it up, and Arm brought in $1.24 billion in the fourth fiscal quarter, up 33.7 percent. Research and development is a big ticket item at ARM, and was actually down 6.5 percent to $546 million, representing 44 percent of revenues. Over the past several years, R&D costs have averaged around 53 percent, just to have a yardstick. Operating income therefore shot through the roof, rising 18.6X to $410 million. Net income was, however, actually off 6.3 percent to $210 million because Arm lost $290 million from equity investments. And this was with a $66 million tax benefit. Net income would probably have been north of $700 million if the stock market had not tanked and Arm saved that tax bennie for some later time.
It looks like Armv9 is driving just shy of 30 percent of royalties in the just-completed quarter:
By our eyes, it looks like Armv7 and old technologies drove somewhat less royalty revenues (call it high 20s in percent terms), and that leaves somewhere north of 45 percent but under 50 percent of royalties being driven by Armv8 devices.
Arm’s use cases have expanded radically between fiscal 2016 and fiscal 2025, as you can see in the chart below:
Cloud and networking compute devices still only account for about 10 percent of royalty revenues for all of fiscal 2024. This is pretty old data shown above and we wish that Arm had updated it for fiscal 2025. Our guess? Cloud and networking is now driving 15 percent to 20 percent of royalty revenues, and will hot 50 percent before too long.
We also wish that Arm had updated this chart for fiscal 2025, but it cuts off at fiscal 2024:
You would think Arm would want to brag a little with CPU chips based on its architecture finally taking off in the datacenter. Go figure.
We will end with some stats. In fiscal 2025, Arm’s partners shipped 30.6 billion chips for all manner of products, and since Arm was founded many decades ago, its partners have shipped a collective 310 billion devices. This is indeed the most pervasive CPU architecture in the world, and there is no surprise that more than 22 million developers write code for Arm chips. That installed base of chips and coders gives Arm a tremendous flywheel for momentum.

• [SillyUsername] 关注ARM被出售给Softbank的政治背景，批评英国政府缺乏远见，并对ARM不再属于英国表示不满。他还提到Boris Johnson曾试图让ARM重回伦敦证券交易所（LSE）。

• [Neywiny] 作为ARM微控制器的用户，对v8和M33的进展表示关注，但对M55的推动力不足感到失望。

• [AtlasBarfed] 关心ARM架构对Linux系统效率的影响，并推测未来CPU发展将更专注于AI处理，而不是传统计算效率的提升。他认为ARM、AMD、Intel在追赶Apple的创新上可能会停滞。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是ARM的定价策略及其市场竞争力。
• 政治因素对科技公司所有权的影响，特别是国家安全和经济利益的考量。
• 对未来CPU发展方向的预测，尤其是AI处理和传统计算的优先级变化。
• 不同用户对ARM产品和策略的个人体验和期望差异。

data.title: Mice grow bigger brains when given this stretch of human DNA
data.author: pavel_lishin
data.article_summary: 研究人员发现了一段人类特有的基因片段（HARE5），当将其植入小鼠体内时，小鼠的大脑体积增加了约6.5%。这一基因片段能增强特定基因的表达，促进神经细胞的生成，从而扩大大脑外层。这项研究发表在《Nature》上，进一步揭示了人类大脑相比灵长类动物为何更大更复杂的部分原因。此前研究曾指出人类加速区域（HARs）可能与大脑发育有关，而HARE5正是其中之一，它在人类版本下能更有效地促进小鼠神经干细胞分裂和神经元生成。不过，目前尚不清楚大脑变大的小鼠是否在认知或记忆上有所提升。这项研究为理解人类大脑演化提供了新视角。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基因编辑实验、动物实验伦理、脑体积与智力的关系以及大众对该话题的文化反应。

不同观点：
• **robwwilliams** 认为6.5%的效应值非常小，且由于发育和技术因素的干扰，结果并不稳健。他指出，即便是基因相同的小鼠，其大脑区域体积的误差系数通常也超过5%。他还质疑转基因是否仅在一个遗传背景（如C57BL/6J小鼠）上进行了测试。

• **ipsum2** 对讨论质量表示不满，指出大部分评论都与文章内容无关，而是流行文化引用和泛泛之谈，认为这种现象降低了讨论的质量。

• **pcthrowaway** 从伦理角度出发，认为使用小鼠进行基因编辑实验以提高其智力是不道德的，特别是考虑到实验后通常会将小鼠“处理掉”。这种做法令人感到悲哀。

• **AngryData** 强调脑体积大小与智力没有很好的相关性，认为如果没有认知测试，单凭脑体积的变化不能说明问题。

• **sshine** 以讽刺的口吻评论，认为即使给小鼠所有人类DNA，它们也不会变成人类。

• **jonplackett** 简单质疑基因编辑后的小鼠是否变得更聪明。

• **metalman** 从文化和社会角度出发，指出基因拼接动物和人类一直是科幻作品中的主题，且有亚文化（如“furry”社区）对此感兴趣。他认为这种实验不可避免，且未来可能会有更多类似实验，包括改变生命体出生后的DNA。

Researchers have identified a genetic dial in the human brain that, when inserted in mice, boosts their brain size by about 6.5%.
Credit: Sergey Bezgodov/Shutterstock
Taking a snippet of genetic code that is unique to humans and inserting it into mice helps the animals to grow bigger brains than usual, according to a report out in
Nature
today
1
.
The slice of code — a stretch of DNA that acts like a dial to turn up the expression of certain genes — expanded the outer layer of the mouse brain by increasing the production of cells that become neurons. The finding could partially explain
how humans evolved such large brains
compared with their primate relatives.
This study goes deeper than previous work that attempted to unpick the genetic mechanisms behind human brain development, says Katherine Pollard, a bioinformatics researcher at the Gladstone Institute of Data Science and Biotechnology in San Francisco, California. “The story is much more complete and convincing,” she says.
The brain expander
How
the human brain
grew to be so big and complex remains a mystery, says Gabriel Santpere Baró, a neuroscientist who studies genomics at the Hospital del Mar Medical Research Institute in Barcelona, Spain. “We still do not have a definitive answer to how the human brain has tripled in size since our split from chimpanzees” during evolution, he says.
How human brains got so big: our cells learned to handle the stress that comes with size
Previous studies
2
,
3
have hinted that human accelerated regions (HARs) — short snippets of the genome that are conserved across mammals, but which underwent rapid change in humans after they evolutionarily diverged from chimpanzees — could be key contributors to brain development and size. But the exact mechanisms that underlie the brain-building effects of HARs are yet to be uncovered, says study co-author Debra Silver, a developmental neurobiologist at Duke University in Durham, North Carolina.
To build a clearer picture, Silver and her colleagues zoomed in on one HAR, called
HARE5
, that they discovered a decade ago
4
. In mice, this snippet of DNA is known to boost the expression of the
Fzd8
gene, one of the big players behind the development and growth of neural cells. The research team compared the effects of
HARE5
in mice, chimpanzees and humans.
When the researchers swapped a human version of
HARE5
into living mice in place of the animals’ own version, the animals’ brains grew to be 6.5% larger than in non-engineered mice by the time they were adults. The brain-enhancing booster was most active in neural stem cells called radial glia, which eventually develop into neurons and other brain cells. The human
HARE5
increased the division and proliferation of the glia, and the cells went on to produce more neurons than they did when under the influence of the mouse version of
HARE5
.
It is so far unclear whether mice that grew larger brains got a boost in cognition or memory, Silver says.

data.title: Show HN: Turn any workflow diagram into compilable, running and stateful code
data.author: yaronsc
data.article_summary:
**Workflow Composer**是一款将工作流图转换为使用开源技术构建的持久应用程序的工具。主要步骤如下：

1. **上传图表**：通过浏览文件、拖放或粘贴（⌘+V / Ctrl+V）方式上传，支持PNG、JPEG、GIF、WebP格式。
2. **选择输出语言**：工具正在加载中，如需帮助，可查阅文档或在Discord社区询问。

该工具还提供了文档、Discord支持、Dapr集成及使用条款等相关信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于通过图表生成代码的工具及其潜力和挑战的讨论

不同观点：
• [raydenvm] 认为这种图表驱动的开发方式类似于2000年代初的UML/RUP时代，并对其能否复活表示怀疑。他指出，现代开发者更倾向于敏捷和代码优先的方法，因为需求变化快，保持图表和代码同步非常困难。
• [mpetrovich] 提供了产品反馈，建议在无需创建账户的情况下展示输入和输出的示例，以便用户更好地理解工具的功能。
• [magicalhippo] 表示对工具主页感到困惑，认为它像是在看一部8集电视剧的第6集，对部分内容熟悉但对整体不理解。
• [bwfan123] 建议将“上传图表”改为“描述图表”，通过LLM生成工作流，让用户编辑，从而简化图表创建过程，增加趣味性。
• [potamic] 对工具如何在市场中竞争和差异化表示关注，指出旗舰LLM也能完成类似任务，这使得新工具的销售变得困难。
• [Rexxar] 询问该工具与Camunda等BPMN工具的区别。
• [sky2224] 对工具嵌入现有代码库的潜力表示兴趣，并提到教授曾预测图表生成代码是软件工程的未来。
• [baumschubser] 支持在软件讨论中使用图表，但质疑所有参与者是否具备理解正式符号的知识，尤其是在非大型企业中。
• [swyx] 指出生成工作流的挑战在于版本控制和错误处理，并询问Diagrid/Dapr与Temporal的比较。
• [revskill] 对生成代码的必要性提出质疑。

补充讨论：
• 图表驱动开发的复兴可能性及其与现代敏捷开发方法的兼容性。
• 用户对工具主页和功能理解的困惑，以及提供示例以增强用户体验的建议。
• 通过自然语言描述生成图表和工作流的想法，以简化用户操作。
• 新工具在LLM和AI应用市场中的竞争和差异化策略。
• 图表工具在不同环境中的适用性和对正式符号的理解需求。
• 代码生成工具的潜在技术挑战，如版本控制和错误处理。

data.title: Project Verona: Fearless Concurrency for Python
data.author: ptx
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了Project Verona团队为Python开发的新所有权模型Lungfish，旨在解决内存管理和并发问题。团队首先通过一个名为FrankenScript的简化语言进行快速原型设计，以探索基于区域的所有权概念，并生成可视化的程序结构图。该原型验证了所有权模型的可行性，并帮助团队向社区解释设计思路。

团队与Microsoft的Faster CPython团队合作，并计划在2025年的Python语言峰会上寻求更广泛的反馈。为了逐步实现新所有权模型，团队首先引入深度不可变性，分为三个部分：深度不可变性模型、循环不可变垃圾管理、以及子解释器间的消息传递集成。深度不可变性是所有权模型的关键，确保并发线程安全共享类型信息。

选择Python是因为其广泛使用和向并发模型转变的趋势，而不用线程和锁的方式是因为当前探索的是子解释器间消息传递。不同于Rust的所有权模型，团队设计的新模型适用于Python的动态类型和现有对象图。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python语言的未来发展方向及相关技术项目的讨论，尤其是在Microsoft结束对Faster CPython项目的支持后，对Verona项目及其他相关技术的影响。

不同观点：
• **fmajid和pjmlp的观点**：关注Microsoft结束对Faster CPython支持后Verona项目的未来，暗示这是一个重要的转折点，可能影响Python并发性能的提升。

• **Findecanor的观点**：通过引用Microsoft研究论文的文件名，指出内部代号"Pyrona"可能暗示Verona项目与CPython的关联，试图从文件细节推测技术方向。

• **mgraczyk的观点**：提到Instagram的Cinder项目，并讨论其与未来Python无GIL（Global Interpreter Lock）方向的兼容性问题，质疑Cinder是否过于老旧以致无法适应新的变化。

• **zenkey的激进观点**：认为Python不应再优先考虑向后兼容，建议推出类似“Python 4”的版本，采用类似Rust的所有权模型，并加强静态类型支持，以适应LLM（大型语言模型）和自动化代码生成技术的发展。

• **froh的观点**：提出希望在Python中实现类似Git的对象树管理方式，以解决并发编程中的问题，强调合并和同步操作的显式性以简化推理。

• **kubb的观点**：批评Python设计上的缺陷，认为其流行后带来的持续修补工作本可以通过更好的初始设计避免，暗示这是一种“先吸引用户，后解决问题”的策略。

• **throwaway81523的观点**：希望Python在2到3的过渡中选择BEAM或其他类似技术，而不是当前的技术路线，表达对现有方向的不满。

• **bgwalter的观点**：提到这是Python并发努力的一部分，指出Faster CPython团队被解雇的事件，并重提子解释器（subinterpreter）方法，质疑Python并发方案的持续性。

• **OutOfHere的观点**：鉴于Microsoft大规模裁员，建议坚持使用类型检查和自由线程的Python，并提出增强类型检查器以检测变量的不安全突变。

• **akkad33的观点**：通过“无畏并发”这一术语联想到其他语言（可能指Rust），暗示Python在并发处理上的不足。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于Python未来的发展方向，尤其是是否应继续强调向后兼容性，以及如何在并发处理和类型系统上做出改进。
- 不同技术方案（如Cinder、Verona、BEAM）之间的兼容性和可行性也是讨论的重要内容。
- 对Microsoft解雇Faster CPython团队的决定及其对Python并发性能研究的影响也是讨论的热点。

43993707.article_content:
Fearless Concurrency for Python
As part of Project Verona, we have been developing a new ownership model for Python, called Lungfish.
This model is designed to provide a safe and efficient way to manage memory and concurrency in Python programs.
This page explains our experiments to develop this approach.
Plan for Python
Quick prototyping in FrankenScript
Modifying a production language is a complex task.
As an initial step, we have been developing a toy language called
FrankenScript
that allows us to quickly prototype our ideas for region-based ownership.
FrankenScript is a small language that is designed to be easy to modify and extend.
It is based on the ideas of ownership and concurrency that we are exploring in Project Verona, but where all the checks are dynamic.
This prototype has given us confidence in the conceptual ideas behind our ownership model, and has allowed us to explore the design space of ownership in a dynamic language.
It has also helped us explain our ideas and the different design decisions to people outside the Project Verona team.
FrankenScript generates a series of mermaid diagrams that show the region structure of the program.  An example of this is shown below:
Engaging with the Python community
Over the last two years, we have been engaging with the Faster CPython team at Microsoft as a sounding board for our ideas.
In May 2025, we will be taking our first steps into the boarder Python community at the
Python Language Summit
.
The presentation that we gave on the Python language summit can be found
here
.
We are seeking feedback from the core developers and broader community behind the language.
Steps to a new ownership model
Building an ownership model for Python is a complex task, and we are taking a step-by-step approach to ensure that we get it right.
The first step is actually to build a concept of deep immutability into Python.  This can be split into three parts:
Deep Immutability: We are starting with a deep immutability model, we have been drafting a
PEP
to describe this model.
The current prototype is in a PR to a fork of CPython 3.12: https://github.com/mjp41/cpython/pull/51
Manage cyclic immutable garbage with reference counting and
atomic reference counting of immutable objects. This will enable objects to be moved between sub-interpreters as they will no longer be managed by the interpreter local cycle collector.
The current prototype is on the following branch: https://github.com/mjp41/cpython/tree/scc, which is based on top of the PR 51 mentioned above.
Integration with message passing between sub-interpreters (
PEP734
).  This will enable us to get parallel performance even though we are technically not losing the GIL.
Deep Immutability is a key part of any ownership model as we need concurrent threads to be able to share type information without risking it being mutated under foot.
As types in Python are mutable objects, we need a way to share these objects between threads.
Once the immutability model is in place, then we can start applying the region-based ownership model to Python to permit safe sharing and transfer of mutable state.
This involves applying the ideas developed in the FrankenScript prototype to Python.
We have made progress on this in our prototyping ideas on CPython, but nothing is ready to try yet.
FAQ
Why Python?
Python is the most popular programming language in the world.
With
PEP703
, aka NoGil or “Free-Threaded” Python, Python is moving to a fully concurrent model.
This means a vast quantity of programmers will be potentially exposed to concurrency issues.
Bringing an ownership model to Python will help to make it easier to write concurrent programs, and to avoid the pitfalls of concurrency.
This is a perfect opportunity to influence the future of Python, and to help make programming experience better for everyone.
Why not threads and locks?
We are initially exploring using message passing between sub-interpreters.  However, we could also apply the region ideas to locks, and provide a lock that gives temporary access to a region of memory associated with that lock.
We have sketched out a design for how to integrate with the full PEP 703 work, but have not attempted to implement that yet.
Why not simply use Rust’s ownership model?
Rust’s ownership model is designed for a statically typed language, and restricts the type of object graphs that can be used in the language.
There is so much existing code in Python that the restrictions of Rust’s ownership model would be too limiting.
We are designing a new ownership model based on regions that is designed to work with Python’s dynamic typing and existing object graphs.
Our approach draws heavily from the experience of languages with ownership models like Rust, Cyclone Encore, and Pony, but is based completely on dynamic checks.  This completely alters the kind of things that can be checked in comparison to a statically typed approach.
What has Project Verona learnt from this work?
Performing

本文介绍了Project Verona团队为Python开发的新所有权模型Lungfish，旨在解决内存管理和并发问题。团队首先通过一个名为FrankenScript的简化语言进行快速原型设计，以探索基于区域的所有权概念，并生成可视化的程序结构图。该原型验证了所有权模型的可行性，并帮助团队向社区解释设计思路。

团队与Microsoft的Faster CPython团队合作，并计划在2025年的Python语言峰会上寻求更广泛的反馈。为了逐步实现新所有权模型，团队首先引入深度不可变性，分为三个部分：深度不可变性模型、循环不可变垃圾管理、以及子解释器间的消息传递集成。深度不可变性是所有权模型的关键，确保并发线程安全共享类型信息。

选择Python是因为其广泛使用和向并发模型转变的趋势，而不用线程和锁的方式是因为当前探索的是子解释器间消息传递。不同于Rust的所有权模型，团队设计的新模型适用于Python的动态类型和现有对象图。

data.title: Climeworks' capture fails to cover its own emissions
data.author: jacobgorm
data.article_summary: Climeworks在冰岛的碳捕集表现远低于预期。自2021年开始运营以来，该公司仅捕集了2,400吨二氧化碳，远低于其宣称的每年4,000吨的捕集能力。其Mammoth捕集厂在运营前十个月仅捕集了105吨，而计划是每年捕集36,000吨。此外，该公司2023年的碳排放达1,700吨，超过其捕集量。由于表现不佳，Orca捕集机在2023年贬值140万美元。Climeworks的冰岛子公司负债近3,000万美元，依赖瑞士母公司资助。尽管未实现最初目标，公司仍计划到2050年捕集10亿吨二氧化碳，并继续吸引全球关注。专家批评碳捕集行业不切实际，而客户购买的碳信用迟迟无法兑现。

不同观点：
• [floydnoel] 认为Climeworks是一个骗局，通过夸大其技术能力来获取投资，并指出美国能源部（DOE）等机构为其提供资金支持是不合理的。他提到Al Gore在2023年的TED演讲中嘲讽了碳捕捉行业，认为这是石油和天然气公司维持其业务的手段。

• [imtringued] 认为即使要进行骗局，也应该更加“诚实”，例如用部分资金购买CO2证书而不使用它们，从而达到类似的效果。他暗示这种项目本质上只是为了获取投资者的资金，设备只是道具。

• [metalman] 从技术角度分析了Climeworks失败的原因，指出其机械效率低下和设备耗能过大。他提到从项目一开始就对其可行性表示怀疑，尤其是缺乏详细的技术细节。他认为Climeworks的实际效果与其宣传相差甚远，甚至可能消耗了比捕捉到的更多的CO2。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Climeworks是否真正有效地实现了碳捕捉，还是只是通过复杂的设备和基础设施来获取资金支持。
• 另一个值得注意的点是美国能源部等机构为何继续支持这种可能存在问题的项目，以及Al Gore对整个碳捕捉行业的公开批评。

Bjartmar Oddur Þeyr Alexandersson
bjartmar@heimildin.is
Valur Grettisson
