data.title: AI models can't tell time or read a calendar, study reveals
data.author: amichail
data.article_summary:
新研究显示，人工智能（AI）在识别模拟时钟时间和确定日历日期方面表现不佳。尽管AI在编写代码、生成图像和创建类人文本等方面表现出色，但它在解读时钟指针位置和进行基本日期计算时经常出错。研究人员在2025年国际表征学习会议（ICLR）上展示了这些发现，并于3月18日在预印本服务器arXiv上发布了研究结果。

研究中，研究人员向多种多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）输入了时钟和日历图像数据集，包括Meta的Llama 3.2-Vision、Anthropic的Claude-3.5 Sonnet、Google的Gemini 2.0和OpenAI的GPT-4o。结果显示，这些模型在识别时钟正确时间和计算日期对应的星期时，成功率分别仅为38.7%和26.3%。

研究指出，AI在处理空间推理任务（如时钟识别）时存在困难，因为它依赖于模式识别而非规则运算。此外，AI在处理需要逻辑和空间推理结合的任务时表现不佳，特别是在训练数据不足的情况下。这项研究强调了在开发AI系统时，需更注重这些基本技能的训练和模型改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于LLM（大型语言模型）在时间感知和知识更新方面的能力和局限性的讨论

不同观点：
• [pona-a] 认为在讨论某个研究时，直接链接到原始研究比博客文章更可取。他提供了相关研究的链接，强调学术来源的可靠性。
• [peacebeard] 分享了关于清醒梦的经验，指出在梦中查看时钟可以发现异常，因为梦中的时间往往是不合逻辑或无法验证的。
• [JoeAltmaier] 补充说，LLM在跟踪日期和日程安排方面也有困难，提到他每晚与一个LLM对话，帮助其理清第二天的日程，但LLM经常弄错日期。
• [A StonesThrow] 通过亲身经历说明LLM在时区转换和当前时间方面的局限性。他提到自己曾与LLM争论伦敦的时间，结果发现LLM无法准确提供当前时间，因为它们的知识库是基于过去的训练数据，无法实时更新。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于LLM在处理实时信息和时间相关任务时的局限性。用户们通过个人经验说明LLM在时间感知和时区转换等任务上的不足，强调了这些模型在动态信息处理方面的局限。
• 另外，也有对信息来源可靠性的讨论，[pona-a] 主张直接引用原始研究以确保信息的准确性和权威性。

44022799.article_content:
AI systems read clocks correctly only 38.7% and calendars only 26.3%
(Image credit: Alamy)
New research has revealed another set of tasks most humans can do with ease that
artificial intelligence
(AI) stumbles over — reading an analogue clock or figuring out the day on which a date will fall.
AI may be able to write code, generate lifelike images, create human-sounding text and even pass exams (
to varying degrees of success
) yet it routinely misinterprets the position of hands on everyday clocks and fails at the basic arithmetic needed for calendar dates.
Researchers revealed these unexpected flaws in a presentation at the 2025 International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR). They also published their findings March 18 on the preprint server
arXiv
, so they have not yet been peer-reviewed .
You may like
AI can handle tasks twice as complex every few months. What does this exponential growth mean for how we use it?
Older AI models show signs of cognitive decline, study shows — but not everyone is entirely convinced
AI is just as overconfident and biased as humans can be, study shows
"Most people can tell the time and use calendars from an early age. Our findings highlight a significant gap in the ability of AI to carry out what are quite basic skills for people," study lead author
Rohit Saxena
, a researcher at the University of Edinburgh,
said in a statement
. These shortfalls must be addressed if AI systems are to be successfully integrated into time-sensitive, real-world applications, such as scheduling, automation and assistive technologies."
To investigate AI's timekeeping abilities, the researchers fed a custom dataset of clock and calendar images into various multimodal large language models (MLLMs), which can process visual as well as textual information. The models used in the study include Meta's Llama 3.2-Vision, Anthropic's Claude-3.5 Sonnet, Google's Gemini 2.0 and OpenAI's GPT-4o.
And the results were poor, with the models being unable to identify the correct time from an image of a clock or the day of the week for a sample date more than half the time.
Related:
Current AI models a 'dead end' for human-level intelligence, scientists agree
Sign up for the Live Science daily newsletter now
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
Contact me with news and offers from other Future brands
Receive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors
However, the researchers have an explanation for AI's surprisingly poor time-reading abilities.
"Early systems were trained based on labelled examples. Clock reading requires something different — spatial reasoning," Saxena said. "The model has to detect overlapping hands, measure angles and navigate diverse designs like Roman numerals or stylized dials. AI recognizing that 'this is a clock' is easier than actually reading it."
Dates proved just as difficult. When given a challenge like "What day will the 153rd day of the year be?," the failure rate was similarly high: AI systems read clocks correctly only 38.7% and calendars only 26.3%.
This shortcoming is similarly surprising because arithmetic is a fundamental cornerstone of computing, but as Saxena explained, AI uses something different. "Arithmetic is trivial for traditional computers but not for large language models. AI doesn't run math algorithms, it predicts the outputs based on patterns it sees in training data," he said. So while it may answer arithmetic questions correctly some of the time, its reasoning isn't consistent or rule-based, and our work highlights that gap."
The project is the latest in a growing body of research that highlights the differences between the ways AI "understands" versus the way humans do. Models derive answers from familiar patterns and excel when there are enough examples in their training data, yet they fail when asked to generalize or use abstract reasoning.
"What for us is a very simple task like reading a clock may be very hard for them, and vice versa," Saxena said.
RELATED STORIES
—
Scientists discover major differences in how humans and AI 'think' — and the implications could be significant
—
If any AI became 'misaligned' then the system would hide it just long enough to cause harm — controlling it is a fallacy
—
Researchers gave AI an 'inner monologue' and it massively improved its performance
The research also reveals the problem AI has when it's trained with limited data — in this case comparatively rare phenomena like leap years or obscure calendar calculations. Even though LLMs have plenty of examples that explain leap years as a concept, that doesn't mean they make the requisite connections required to complete a visual task.
The research highlights both the need for more targeted examples in training data and the need to rethink how AI handles the combination of logical and spatial reasoning, especially in tasks it doesn't encounter often.

data.title: Reflecting on Software Engineering Handbook
data.author: yusufaytas
data.article_summary:
《软件工程手册》发布于2025年5月18日，回顾了该书从发布到一周年的历程。作者们在2024年5月完成了这个历时两年的项目，并为此庆祝。尽管最初对该书寄予厚望，希望它成为软件工程领域的指南，但一年后发现其影响远不如预期。

该书内容受到了一些读者的好评，认为其提供了实用的见解，但书名和标题存在问题。书名中的“手册”误导了读者，因为内容远超手册的范畴，更像是一本全面的指南。同时，书名过于泛泛，在竞争激烈的技术书籍市场中难以脱颖而出。

销售数据揭示了残酷的现实。尽管在Google上的销量占比最高，但收入微薄，主要收入来自亚马逊。初期销售后，销量迅速下滑，大部分Google上的销量来自土耳其的学生折扣码，实际收入几乎为零。

总的来说，该书在内容上得到了认可，但市场表现不佳，未达到预期收入。

44022529.article_content:
Reflecting on Software Engineering Handbook
Published 2025-05-18
One year. May 2024. Back then, we were riding high, celebrating the launch of this
Software Engineering Handbook
with an amazing
trip to Iceland
. Five days of glaciers and waterfalls, finally enjoying the fact that we finished up a two year project. We thought we’d cracked it, pouring our hard won experience into a guide for
anyone navigating the software engineering business
. Our book was born from the trenches, covering everything from job offers to handling conflicts, managing projects to recovering from the inevitable screw-ups. We thought we were giving people the map we never had.
Fast forward a year, and the reality check hits harder than a Reykjavik winter. Never been there in winter but assuming it’s cold. Let’s skip the bullshit and dissect why this thing didn’t exactly become the bible of software engineering we envisioned. But first off, let’s see a few hits and misses.
Hits and Misses
Let me be fair.  The book wasn’t without its merits. We were genuinely humbled and encouraged by the overwhelmingly positive feedback from a few readers, especially regarding the content. People genuinely found it valuable. Here’s a review that made me really happy.
I finished the book and really enjoyed it. It’s packed with essential, practical insights that you wouldn’t typically find collected in one place. It reminded me of ‘Crucial Conversations,’ but more comprehensive. Just having the ‘Contents’ alone would be useful to anyone looking to learn these topics. Great job, it turned out really well!
However, two key issues emerged that, in hindsight, were significant headwinds:
The “Handbook” Misnomer:
We called it a “Handbook,” but the final product evolved into something much more substantial – definitely more of a full guide than a quick reference. Despite our best efforts to trim it down during writing and editing, its length contradicted the title, potentially setting the wrong expectation.
A Generic Title Problem:
While the main title resonated, the overall name felt a bit too generic. In the incredibly crowded marketplace of technical books, standing out is crucial, and our generic name likely hindered that.
So, while the content itself held up and was appreciated by those who read it, these initial structural and naming decisions were definite drawbacks. The data, as always, is brutally honest. Let’s take a look.
The Hard Numbers
The data from these charts lays it out pretty clearly what happened and when.
First, the vanity numbers: Units Share By Marketplace.
Google
‘s “winning” with 48.7%,
Amazon
trailing slightly at 47.7%.
Apple
‘s a rounding error at 3.5%. Looks like we moved some copies, right? Wrong.
Then, the only metric that actually pays the bills: royalty shares by marketplace. Amazon coughs up $434. Apple manages $63. Google? A pathetic $49. That massive unit share on Google smells, no?
The monthly royalty chart tells the real story of our fleeting moment in the sun. That initial spike in July 2024? That wasn’t just the official launch; it was the immediate, albeit small, wave from our initial LinkedIn posts and whatever other noise we made. We saw around 40 quick sales. Then, reality hit, and it nosedived. The smaller bump in November ’24 was likely the Hacker News echo. After that? A flatline, with Amazon barely keeping the lights on.
Looking at top countries by market place, Turkey is bizarrely dominant on Google. The US comes in second, a more balanced spread. You might say this isn’t a surprise given that both authors are Turkish. Perhaps. Perhaps. Perhaps.
But top countries by royalty paints a different picture. The US is the only country that generated any real (and I use that term loosely) income, mostly through Amazon. Turkey? Nada. This Google situation is clearly a red herring.
Software Engineering Handbook monthly total units sold
The monthly total unit sold chart confirms the initial small burst in June 2024 (reflecting those immediate post-launch sales), followed by the July peak. Then, the slow bleed. Those smaller December bumps, coinciding with Turkey’s Google unit spikes, point to something specific.
The punchline? That massive Google unit share, especially in Turkey around December, generated zero revenue. We handed out discount codes to Bilkent University students. This is the university we both studied at. Charity, not actual market demand. Those initial 40 or so sales post-launch were the closest we got to organic traction before the long, slow decline.
So, the truth is stark: the initial small ripple from our immediate network quickly died. The only real sales channel was Amazon, and even that was underwhelming. The Google numbers are a misleading artifact of a student discount.
The brutal truth? We paid out $1500 to our editor, Courtney Goldsmith (who, to be fair, did a damn good job polishing this book), and we’re nowhere close to seeing that money back. That’s the bottom line. All this talk about units
44022529.article_summary:
《软件工程手册》发布于2025年5月18日，回顾了该书从发布到一周年的历程。作者们在2024年5月完成了这个历时两年的项目，并为此庆祝。尽管最初对该书寄予厚望，希望它成为软件工程领域的指南，但一年后发现其影响远不如预期。

该书内容受到了一些读者的好评，认为其提供了实用的见解，但书名和标题存在问题。书名中的“手册”误导了读者，因为内容远超手册的范畴，更像是一本全面的指南。同时，书名过于泛泛，在竞争激烈的技术书籍市场中难以脱颖而出。

销售数据揭示了残酷的现实。尽管在Google上的销量占比最高，但收入微薄，主要收入来自亚马逊。初期销售后，销量迅速下滑，大部分Google上的销量来自土耳其的学生折扣码，实际收入几乎为零。

总的来说，该书在内容上得到了认可，但市场表现不佳，未达到预期收入。

data.title: Apple card disabled my iCloud, App Store, and Apple ID accounts (2021)
data.author: thanatosmin
data.article_summary: 一位用户在尝试更新Mac上的应用程序时遇到错误，随后发现其iCloud、App Store和Apple ID账户被禁用。尽管最初以为是系统故障，但问题逐渐扩展到Apple Music和Calendar等服务。经过多次联系Apple支持，用户最终发现问题源于其Apple Card与银行账户的自动支付失败。由于用户未及时处理一笔与购买M1 MacBook Pro相关的贸易优惠，Apple Card被标记为逾期，导致所有关联账户被禁用。尽管问题最终解决，用户对Apple未明确告知问题及迅速采取极端措施感到担忧，尤其是涉及账户和数据的安全。Apple的邮件中存在信息不准确和误导，且Apple Card协议未提及相关技术细节。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果公司处理未支付账单及相关账户限制的合理性，以及大科技公司在客户服务和账户管理方面的普遍问题。

不同观点：
• **支持苹果立场**：一些用户认为苹果在此情况下采取的行动是合理的。例如，用户jms703指出，苹果在采取行动前已发出通知，且用户未回应或履行其付款义务，因此限制账户访问是合乎逻辑的结果。这种观点强调用户的失误和责任。

• **批评苹果做法**：其他用户，如josephcsible，认为苹果的做法过于严厉，特别是将用户过去购买的内容作为未支付账单的抵押品。这种观点将苹果的行为比作不合理的商业行为，类似于其他行业中看似荒谬的惩罚措施。

• **生态系统风险**：Zak和GuestFAUniverse等用户关注依赖单一公司生态系统的风险，指出如果出现问题，用户可能会失去对多个服务的访问。这种观点强调多样化选择的重要性，避免因一个失误而失去所有服务。

• **大公司客户服务问题**：blindriver和joshstrange批评大科技公司在客户服务方面的不足，认为这些公司由于垄断地位而缺乏改善客户服务的动力。他们建议应有法律强制这些公司提供更好的支持服务。

• **个人经历与体验**：joshstrange分享了个人与苹果支持互动的积极体验，但也指出了支付问题通知不清的困扰。这种观点提供了一线希望，认为虽然有问题，但支持团队的表现可能会有所帮助。

补充讨论：
• **用户责任与遗忘**：edwinjm和amelius指出，用户应对自己的付款负责，不应依赖公司提醒。同时，有用户建议公司内部应有类似“权力分立”的机制以防止滥用权力。

• **避免特定产品**：kaonwarb和xyst表示，这些故事使他们决定避免使用苹果卡或其他与日常生活工具紧密相关的金融产品，转而购买替代品以避免被“围墙花园”锁定。

争议焦点：苹果是否有权在未支付账单的情况下限制用户对已购买内容的访问，以及大科技公司在处理此类问题时的客户服务质量。

March  1, 2021
Apple Card disabled my iCloud, App Store, and Apple ID accounts
About ten days ago, when I went to update a few apps in the App Store on my Mac, I was met with a curious error.
The internet is filled with stories from people whose Google accounts were locked for unexplained reasons, causing them to lose all of their data, including years of email, so I was somewhat concerned. But I’d never heard of similar cases involving Apple’s services, and I wouldn’t expect such behavior from a customer-focused company like Apple, so I figured it was a glitch and made a mental note to try again later.
The next day, Music.app stopped working.
Now I was genuinely worried. I checked my phone and neither the App Store nor Apple Music would work there, either. A few minutes later, Calendar popped up an error – it had stopped syncing. I immediately tried to call Apple Support from my Mac, but Apple’s Handoff feature had been disabled as well.
The first person I spoke to at Apple spent a while researching the issue and then told me there was nothing she could do but escalate the issue, and that I should expect a call
“hopefully”
within the next day. I asked what the problem might be, and she seemed as confused as I was. Although some Apple services were still working, like iMessage (thank God) and Photos, I was terrified that more services would suddenly become inaccessible or that I would lose the considerable amount of data I have stored in iCloud.
A couple of days later, I became impatient and contacted Apple Support again. This time, the representative mumbled something about Apple Card before saying that he also had no power to help me. Apple ID was a different department, he said, and they could only be contacted by email. He emailed them. I continued to wait.
The next time I tried to use my Apple Card, it was declined. Strange. I checked the Wallet app, and the balance was below the limit. I remembered the Apple support representative mumbling about Apple Card, so I did some digging through my email to see if I could find a connection.
As it turns out, my bank account number changed in January, causing Apple Card autopay to fail. Then the Apple Store made a charge on the card. Less than fifteen days after that, my App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, and Apple ID accounts had all been disabled by Apple Card.
So what happened?
#
In mid-January, I bought an M1 MacBook Pro. The checkout flow offered a trade-in credit for an old MacBook Pro I had laying around. The Apple Store said I would receive a “trade-in kit” by mail and then have two weeks to send the old MacBook to Apple. Sounds easy, and definitely a very Apple-like experience.
But the trade-in kit never arrived. I had forgotten about it. When I received an email in mid-February asking about the trade-in, I responded (as it had invited me to do) explaining that I never received the kit and asked for another one. I didn’t get a response.
Very soon after, it seems that Apple simply added the amount of the credit I received when I purchased the M1 MacBook Pro to my Apple Card balance. Normally, this wouldn’t be a problem. Imagine if I had used any other credit card – it would have just been an ordinary charge. But because it was the Apple Store and Apple Card, apparently, things escalated very quickly.
On February 15th, Apple sent me this email:
Action Required: Apple Card
From: Apple
payment@apple.com
Reply-to:
preceivables@apple.com
We’ve been unable to collect full payment for your new iPhone. As a result, we will block the device on the order from further access to the Apple iTunes and Mac App stores, and disable all accounts associated with the device purchased on the order.
To resolve this issue, please call 1-877-255-5923 to speak with an Apple Card Specialist at Goldman Sachs. Once the issue has been resolved, reply to this email so we can charge your card for the difference in value.
For your protection, do not submit credit card information via email.
It appears as though charges from Apple are special, and if your account is not 100% current, Apple will quickly take drastic action. Unfortunately, this email got lost in my inbox and I didn’t see it until I went looking. But it is extremely concerning for several reasons.
Apple says it will hold my Apple accounts hostage in order to collect a payment.
It says it is related to an iPhone when it was actually regarding a MacBook Pro. And iTunes no longer exists. The lack of attention to detail is not great given the seriousness of the threat that follows.
It was sent when Apple Card was only a few days past due.
It suggests that charges by Apple on Apple Card are different from other purchases, and this can have serious consequences. (Also: the Apple Card agreement does not mention this technicality.)
After fixing the Apple Card issue, I replied to the email as it says, and received this in response:
Great.
By this point, Apple Support had been unable to help me – or to even identify the issue. My App S

data.title: The X220 ThinkPad Is the Best Laptop in the World
data.author: exiguus
data.article_summary: 《X220 ThinkPad是世界上最优秀的笔记本电脑》一文认为，X220是迄今为止最完美的笔记本电脑，其硬件设计几乎无懈可击。相比现代笔记本为了轻薄和设计美感而牺牲实用性和可修复性，X220凭借其坚固的做工、丰富的接口、经典的键盘、可靠的电池续航和极高的可修复性脱颖而出。文章详细介绍了X220的规格和优点：它的构建质量如坦克般坚固，接口齐全（包括3个USB接口、DisplayPort、VGA、以太网等），键盘手感极佳且功能齐全，电池可轻松更换，续航表现也非常出色。尽管现代设备在轻薄和电池技术上有所进步，但X220在实用性和耐用性上仍无可比拟。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：X220笔记本电脑的优缺点及与其他现代笔记本（如Framework Laptop）的比较

不同观点：
• foobarbecue认为X220t由于其可书写的触摸屏功能更优越，尤其在特定使用场景（如挂在墙上使用）时表现出色。该用户强调其实际使用体验，并认为X220t在物理交互方面非常实用。

• camgunz赞赏X220的输入系统、存储灵活性、耐用性以及可更换部件等优点，但也指出其显示技术过时（1366x768分辨率）和外部分辨率受限（2560x1600）的问题。此外，他认为现代软件对X220的CPU来说过于沉重，但提出通过硬件升级（如Raspberry Pi 5 CM）来解决的设想。

• exiguus拥有多台X220及其前后代机型（X201、X230），并表示X220因其经典设计（如蓝色Enter键）和耐用性而成为其最爱。然而，他也提到风扇问题和过热现象，并说明已将X220作为"假期"笔记本使用，运行FreeBSD和Sway。

• varbhat质疑X220被誉为"最佳"笔记本的说法，认为其性能无法与现代笔记本相比，并提出对现代开放源代码友好、电池寿命长、易于维修和硬件优良的笔记本的需求。同时，提到Framework笔记本可能符合这些标准，但未完全确定。

• eviks对X220的键盘布局提出批评，认为其不符合人体工程学，且屏幕分辨率不佳，不能称为最佳。

• latentcall表示其i5处理器的X220性能下降，运行速度缓慢，需要借助Firefox插件来改善浏览体验。

• dvfjsdhgfv指出Framework笔记本在iFixit可修复性评分上高于Thinkpad，并提到Framework具有物理麦克风关闭开关，而X220没有。

• kh_hk简短表示更偏好x60系列。

• bigyabai赞同kh_hk的观点，认为X201性能强大，若能升级高分辨率屏幕会继续使用。

• baal80spam反对"最佳笔记本"的说法，认为如同没有最佳汽车一样，不存在最佳笔记本。

• ungreased0675不理解追求超薄轻便笔记本的趋势，更倾向于厚重、耐用且接口丰富的笔记本，以应对多种使用场景和旅行需求。

补充讨论：
• X220的耐用性和可升级性被广泛认可，但其显示技术和性能已逐渐落后于现代需求。
• 不同用户对"最佳笔记本"的定义存在差异，部分用户关注物理交互和耐用性，而其他用户则更重视性能和显示效果。
• Framework笔记本作为现代替代品被多次提及，特别是在可修复性和隐私保护方面具有优势。
• 键盘布局和屏幕分辨率是争议的焦点，部分用户对X220的这些方面提出批评。

44022677.article_content:
The X220 ThinkPad is the Best Laptop in the World
2023-09-26
The X220 ThinkPad is the greatest laptop ever made and you’re wrong if you think otherwise. No laptop hardware has since surpassed the nearly perfect build of the X220. New devices continue to get thinner and more fragile. Useful ports are constantly discarded for the sake of “design”. Functionality is no longer important to manufacturers. Repairability is purposefully removed to prevent users from truly “owing” their hardware.
It’s a mess out there. But thank goodness I still have my older, second-hand X220.
Specs
Before I get into the details explaining why this laptop is the very best of its kind, let’s first take a look at my machine’s basic specifications:
CPU: Intel i7-2640M (4) @ 3.500GHz
GPU: Intel 2nd Generation Core Processor
Memory: 16GB DDR3
OS: Arch Linux / OpenBSD
Resolution: 1366x768
With that out of the way, I will break down my thoughts on the X220 into five major sections: Build quality, available ports, the keyboard, battery life, and repairability.
Build Quality
The X220 (like most of Lenovo’s older X/T models) is built like a tank. Although the inner pieces are sourced from mostly plastic, the device is still better equipped to handle drops and mishandling compared to that of more fragile devices (such as the MacBook Air or Framework). This is made further impressive since the X220 is actually composed of many smaller interconnected pieces (more on this later).
A good litmus test I perform on most laptops is the “corner test”. You grab the base corner of a laptop in its open state. The goal is to see if the device displays any noticeable give or flex. In the X220’s case: it feels rock solid. The base remains stiff and bobbing the device causes no movement on the opened screen. I’m aware that holding a laptop in this position is certainly not a normal use case, but knowing it is built well enough to do so speaks volumes of its construction.
The X220 is also
not
a lightweight laptop. This might be viewed as a negative for most users, but I actually prefer it. I often become too cautious and end up “babying” thinner laptops out of fear of breakage. A minor drop from even the smallest height will severely damage these lighter devices. I have no such worries with my X220.
As for the laptop’s screen and resolution: your mileage may vary. I have zero issues with the default display or the smaller aspect ratio. I wrote about how I
stopped using an external monitor
, so I might be a little biased.
Overall, this laptop is a device you can snatch up off your desk, whip into your travel bag and be on your way. The rugged design and bulkier weight help put my mind at ease - which is something I can’t say for newer laptop builds.
Ports
I don’t think I need to explain how valuable it is to have functional ports on a laptop. Needing to carrying around a bunch of dongles for ports that should already be
on the device
just seems silly.
The X220 comes equipped with:
3 USB ports (one of those being USB3 on the i7 model)
DisplayPort
VGA
Ethernet
SD Card Reader
3.5mm Jack
Ultrabay (SATA)
Wi-Fi hardware kill-switch
Incredibly versatile and ready for anything I throw at it!
Keyboard
The classic ThinkPad keyboards are simply that: classic. I don’t think anyone could argue against these keyboards being the golden standard for laptops. It’s commendable how Lenovo managed to package so much functionality into such a small amount of real estate. Most modern laptops lack helpful keys such as
Print Screen
,
Home
,
End
, and
Scroll Lock
.
They’re also an absolute
joy
to type on. The fact that so many people go out of their way to mod X230 ThinkPad models with X220 keyboards should tell you something… Why Lenovo moved away from these keyboards will always baffle me. (I know
why
they did it - I just think it’s stupid).
Did I mention these classic keyboards come with the extremely useful Trackpoint as well?
Battery Life
Author’s Note:
This section is very subjective. The age, quality, and size of the X220’s battery can have a massive impact on benchmarks. I should also mention that I run very lightweight operating systems and use DWM as opposed to a heavier desktop environment. Just something to keep in mind.
The battery life on my own X220 is fantastic. I have a brand-new 9-cell that lasts for roughly 5-6 hours of daily work. Obviously these numbers don’t come close to the incredible battery life of Apple’s M1/M2 chip devices, but it’s still quite competitive against other “newer” laptops on the market.
Although, even if the uptime was lower than 5-6 hours, you have the ability to carry extra batteries with you. The beauty of swapping out your laptop’s battery without needing to
open up
the device itself is fantastic. Others might whine about the annoyance of carrying an extra battery in their travel bag, but doing so is completely
optional
. A core part of what makes the X220 so wonderful is user control and choice. The X220’s battery is another great example

• camgunz赞赏X220的输入系统、存储灵活性、耐用性以及可更换部件等优点，但也指出其显示技术过时（1366x768分辨率）和外部分辨率受限（2560x1600）的问题。此外，他认为现代软件对X220的CPU来说过于沉重，但提出通过硬件升级（如Raspberry Pi 5 CM）来解决的设想。

• exiguus拥有多台X220及其前后代机型（X201、X230），并表示X220因其经典设计（如蓝色Enter键）和耐用性而成为其最爱。然而，他也提到风扇问题和过热现象，并说明已将X220作为"假期"笔记本使用，运行FreeBSD和Sway。

• varbhat质疑X220被誉为"最佳"笔记本的说法，认为其性能无法与现代笔记本相比，并提出对现代开放源代码友好、电池寿命长、易于维修和硬件优良的笔记本的需求。同时，提到Framework笔记本可能符合这些标准，但未完全确定。

• eviks对X220的键盘布局提出批评，认为其不符合人体工程学，且屏幕分辨率不佳，不能称为最佳。

• latentcall表示其i5处理器的X220性能下降，运行速度缓慢，需要借助Firefox插件来改善浏览体验。

• dvfjsdhgfv指出Framework笔记本在iFixit可修复性评分上高于Thinkpad，并提到Framework具有物理麦克风关闭开关，而X220没有。

• kh_hk简短表示更偏好x60系列。

• bigyabai赞同kh_hk的观点，认为X201性能强大，若能升级高分辨率屏幕会继续使用。

• baal80spam反对"最佳笔记本"的说法，认为如同没有最佳汽车一样，不存在最佳笔记本。

• ungreased0675不理解追求超薄轻便笔记本的趋势，更倾向于厚重、耐用且接口丰富的笔记本，以应对多种使用场景和旅行需求。

补充讨论：
• X220的耐用性和可升级性被广泛认可，但其显示技术和性能已逐渐落后于现代需求。
• 不同用户对"最佳笔记本"的定义存在差异，部分用户关注物理交互和耐用性，而其他用户则更重视性能和显示效果。
• Framework笔记本作为现代替代品被多次提及，特别是在可修复性和隐私保护方面具有优势。
• 键盘布局和屏幕分辨率是争议的焦点，部分用户对X220的这些方面提出批评。

data.title: Squirrel (Programming Language)
data.author: 90s_dev
data.article_summary: Squirrel是一种由Alberto Demichelis设计的高级脚本编程语言，具有面向对象、命令式、函数式和协程等特性。它旨在满足视频游戏等应用的实时要求，具有轻量级和跨平台的特点。Squirrel使用了类似C语言的语法，但受Lua启发，支持动态类型、高阶函数、尾递归和异常处理等功能。其编译器和虚拟机由约7000行C++代码实现。Squirrel被广泛应用于多个游戏和软件项目中，如《Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: My Life as a King》、《Left 4 Dead 2》、《Portal 2》以及Code::Blocks等。该语言最初于2003年发布，并于2010年将许可证更改为MIT许可证。

data.title: OpenAI's planned data center in Abu Dhabi would be bigger than Monaco
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: OpenAI计划在阿布扎比开发一个占地10平方英里、容量达5千兆瓦的数据中心园区，这可能是全球最大的AI基础设施项目之一。该设施将由OpenAI与阿布扎比科技集团G42合作建设，是OpenAI雄心勃勃的Stargate项目的一部分，该项目还涉及SoftBank和Oracle，目标是在全球建立大型数据中心。虽然OpenAI在美国德州的第一个Stargate园区容量为1.2千兆瓦，但阿布扎比的园区将扩大四倍多。该项目引发了美国一些立法者的担忧，因为G42与中国企业和实体有联系，可能导致美国技术外流。随后，微软对G42投资15亿美元，以加强其在该地区的影响力。

44022575.article_content:
OpenAI is poised to help develop a staggering 5-gigawatt data center campus in Abu Dhabi, positioning the company as a primary anchor tenant in what could become one of the world’s largest AI infrastructure projects, according to a new
Bloomberg report
.
The facility would reportedly span an astonishing 10 square miles and consume power equivalent to five nuclear reactors, dwarfing any existing AI infrastructure announced by OpenAI or its competitors. (OpenAI has not yet returned TechCrunch’s request for comment, but to put that into perspective, that’s bigger than Monaco.)
The UAE project, developed in partnership with G42 — an Abu Dhabi-based tech conglomerate — is part of OpenAI’s ambitious Stargate project, a joint venture announced in January that could see OpenAI, SoftBank, and Oracle build massive data centers around the globe stocked with powerful computer chips to support AI development.
While OpenAI’s first Stargate campus in the U.S. — already under development in Abilene, Texas — is expected to reach 1.2 gigawatts, this Middle Eastern counterpart would more than quadruple that capacity.
The project is emerging amid broader AI ties between the U.S. and UAE that have been years in the making, and have made some lawmakers nervous.
OpenAI’s relationship with the UAE dates back to a
2023 partnership
with G42 aimed at driving AI adoption in the Middle East. During a talk earlier that same year in Abu Dhabi, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman praised the UAE, saying it “has been talking about AI
since before it was cool
.”
As with much of the AI world, these relationships are… complicated. Founded in 2018, G42 is chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE’s national security advisor and younger brother of the country’s ruler. Its embrace by OpenAI raised concerns in late 2023 among U.S. officials, who feared that G42 could enable China’s government to
gain access to advanced U.S. technology
.

data.title: Encoding Hangeul, Koreas writing system
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary:
韩文（Hangeul）是朝鲜语的现代书写系统，由朝鲜王朝第四代国王世宗大王于1443年创制。在此之前，韩语使用汉字（Hanja）书写。即使在韩文创制后，汉字仍在正式和学术场合中使用数世纪。

韩文是音节文字，每个音节由称为“字母”（Jamo）的字符组成，共有11,172种可能的音节组合。学习韩文只需掌握68个不同形状的字母及其组合规则，通常在60-90分钟内即可掌握基础。

韩文字母在Unicode中有独立的编码值，范围从U+1100到U+11C2。一个韩文音节包括首辅音、中元音和尾辅音。例如，“한”可以分解为：首辅音“ㅎ”，中元音“ㅏ”，尾辅音“ㄴ”。没有尾辅音的音节，如“자”，则无需尾部。

Unicode还定义了从U+AC00到U+D7A3的所有韩文音节组合，这些音节可以映射回各个字母组合。不过，实际使用中，韩文文本通常直接使用预组合的音节，而不是单独的字母。

44021758.article_content:
Introduction
Hangeul (한글) is the modern writing system for the Korean language, created in 1443 by King Sejong the great, the fourth king of the Joseon dynasty
1
. Before its invention, Korean was written using Hanja (한자) — Chinese characters adapted for Korean. Even after Hangeul’s creation, Hanja remained in regular use for centuries, particularly in formal and scholarly contexts
2
.
Hangeul is a syllabic writing system where each syllable is composed of letters called Jamo (자모). These Jamo function like Latin letters, each representing an individual sound. There are a total of 11,172 syllabic combinations of Jamo which can be used to form Hangeul
3
.
However, learning Hangeul doesn’t require memorizing thousands of combinations. Instead, one only needs to learn the 68 different Jamo shapes and rules governing the construction of Hangeul. This is much easier than it sounds with the basics of the Korean alphabet being able to be learned within 60-90 minutes.
This post explores how Hangeul is encoded in Unicode, a universal standard that assigns unique values to characters across all languages
4
. It also delves into the mathematical operations used to construct and deconstruct individual Jamo from encoded Hangeul.
Hangeul, Jamo, and Unicode
A Korean syllable consists of a lead consonant, a medial vowel, and a tail consonant. For example,
한 (han) can be deconstructed like so:
ㅎ (h) is the lead consonant.
ㅏ (a) is the medial vowel.
ㄴ (n) is the tail consonant.
자 (ja) can be deconstructed like so:
ㅈ (j) is the lead consonant.
ㅏ (a) is the medial vowel.
There is no tail consonant.
Syllables starting with an initial vowel, for example 안 (an), must be prefixed with ㅇ (eung), a special lead consonant that produces no sound.
There are 19 different lead consonants ranging between Unicode values U+1100 and U+1112. There are 21 different vowels ranging between Unicode values U+1161 and U+1175. Finally, there are 27 tail consonants ranging between Unicode values U+11A8 and U+11C2 + a null consonant used when there is no tail. This range of Unicode is called the Hangeul Jamo block.
Below is a set of tables providing each Jamo, its canonical order, as well as its Unicode value. When Jamo are used in combination with each other, they change their shape, size, and positions slightly to fit into a single Hangeul. Unicode has a second range of Jamo characters called “Hangeul Compatibility Jamo” starting at U+3130 which represent the initial and final consonants with the same Unicode codepoint as opposed to the Hangeul Jamo block which assigns them separate codepoints
5
. These compatibility Jamo typically render much more clearer.
The table below shows both, the conjoining Jamo as well as the [compatibility Jamo] with the character reference hex value referring to the former

. Depending on your browser, both Jamo may render the same.

44021758.article_summary:
韩文（Hangeul）是朝鲜语的现代书写系统，由朝鲜王朝第四代国王世宗大王于1443年创制。在此之前，韩语使用汉字（Hanja）书写。即使在韩文创制后，汉字仍在正式和学术场合中使用数世纪。

韩文是音节文字，每个音节由称为“字母”（Jamo）的字符组成，共有11,172种可能的音节组合。学习韩文只需掌握68个不同形状的字母及其组合规则，通常在60-90分钟内即可掌握基础。

韩文字母在Unicode中有独立的编码值，范围从U+1100到U+11C2。一个韩文音节包括首辅音、中元音和尾辅音。例如，“한”可以分解为：首辅音“ㅎ”，中元音“ㅏ”，尾辅音“ㄴ”。没有尾辅音的音节，如“자”，则无需尾部。

Unicode还定义了从U+AC00到U+D7A3的所有韩文音节组合，这些音节可以映射回各个字母组合。不过，实际使用中，韩文文本通常直接使用预组合的音节，而不是单独的字母。

data.title: Push Ifs Up and Fors Down
data.author: goranmoomin
data.article_summary:
这篇文章提出了两个编程优化建议：“向上推if条件”和“向下推for循环”。

1. **向上推if条件**：将函数内部的if条件移到调用者处处理，可以简化函数逻辑，集中控制流，减少重复检查，并通过类型或断言确保前提条件。这样可以简化复杂的分支逻辑，更容易发现冗余和无效的分支。

2. **向下推for循环**：将对多个对象的操作以“批处理”方式进行，而不是在循环内逐个处理。这样可以分摊启动成本，提高性能，甚至实现向量化处理。此方法在处理大量数据时尤为有效，能显著提升性能。

这两个建议可以结合使用，通过集中控制流和批处理操作，提高代码的清晰度和性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：代码中条件语句（ifs）和循环（loops）的放置位置及其对性能、可读性和可维护性的影响。

不同观点：
• Waterluvian认为条件语句用于修剪程序树，应尽早修剪以减少不必要的工作。他将条件语句视为决定哪些工作不需要做，而循环则是实际的“工作”。
• Andyg_blog建议将条件语句尽量靠近输入源，以在核心逻辑前做出尽可能多的保证，尤其是通过类型编码来实现。
• Kazinator反对将所有条件语句移到调用者，特别是在函数被多次调用或条件与函数核心逻辑密切相关的情况下。他指出这种做法可能与良好的程序组织相冲突。
• Layer8指出通过多态性可以消除条件语句，将决策与执行分离，从而在改变决策时只需修改一处。
• Password4321提到代码复杂度扫描工具最终会迫使条件语句下放，与一些文章推荐的做法相反。
• Shawnz认为将条件语句放在被调用函数中有助于防止调用者错误地执行操作顺序，特别是在需要保证幂等性或事务边界时。
• Krick认为没有通用规则，但倾向于将条件语句下放以避免重复，并在性能允许的情况下将循环上推以利用函数组合。
• Kuyawa强调为了代码可读性和封装性，应将条件和循环下放。
• Dcre引用了Sandi Metz的观点，认为将逻辑分叉上移有助于处理多层传递的标志。
• Sparkie提到在某些情况下，为了利用SIMD，将分支逻辑替换为无分支代码可以提高性能。
• Rco8786对这种规则持怀疑态度，认为其高度依赖于具体情境，例外情况太多。
• Aeyxen指出在数据管道、游戏引擎和大型Web基础设施中，局部代码清晰度不能牺牲全局吞吐量或可维护性。在处理热循环时，尽早退出可以提升性能。
• Gnabgib提到之前的一个讨论，提供了更多背景。
• Janosch_123建议将条件语句作为守卫语句放在顶部，并将断言添加到函数末尾。
• NeroK指出某些例子中条件语句的上推下放可能并没有实际的好处，具体实现需要考虑实际逻辑。

补充讨论：
• 条件语句和循环的放置需要权衡代码可读性、性能优化和可维护性。
• 多态性和函数组合在消除条件语句和优化循环方面提供了替代方案。
• 具体实现需要根据项目需求和性能考虑进行调整，没有一成不变的规则。

44013157.article_content:
Push Ifs Up And Fors Down
Nov 15, 2023
A short note on two related rules of thumb.
Push Ifs Up
If there’s an
if
condition inside a function, consider
if it could be moved to the caller instead:
// GOOD
fn
frobnicate
(walrus: Walrus) {
...
}
// BAD
fn
frobnicate
(walrus:
Option
<Walrus>) {
let
walrus
=
match
walrus {
Some
(it) => it,
None
=>
return
,
};
...
}
As in the example above, this often comes up with preconditions: a
function might check precondition inside and “do nothing” if it
doesn’t hold, or it could push the task of precondition checking to
its caller, and enforce via types (or an assert) that the
precondition holds. With preconditions especially, “pushing up” can
become viral, and result in fewer checks overall, which is one
motivation for this rule of thumb.
Another motivation is that control flow and
if
s are
complicated, and are a source of bugs. By pushing
if
s
up, you often end up centralizing control flow in a single function,
which has a complex branching logic, but all the actual work is
delegated to straight line subroutines.
If
you have complex control flow, better to fit it on a
screen in a single function, rather than spread throughout the file.
What’s more, with all the flow in one place it often is possible to
notice redundancies and dead conditions. Compare:
fn
f
() {
if
foo && bar {
if
foo {
}
else
{
}
}
}
fn
g
() {
if
foo && bar {
h
()
}
}
fn
h
() {
if
foo {
}
else
{
}
}
For
f
, it’s much easier to notice a dead branch than
for a combination of
g
and
h
!
A related pattern here is what I call “dissolving enum” refactor.
Sometimes, the code ends up looking like this:
enum
E
{
Foo
(
i32
),
Bar
(
String
),
}
fn
main
() {
let
e
=
f
();
g
(e)
}
fn
f
()
->
E {
if
condition {
E::
Foo
(x)
}
else
{
E::
Bar
(y)
}
}
fn
g
(e: E) {
match
e {
E::
Foo
(x) =>
foo
(x),
E::
Bar
(y) =>
bar
(y)
}
}
There are two branching instructions here and, by pulling them up,
it becomes apparent that it is the exact same condition, triplicated
(the third time reified as a data structure):
fn
main
() {
if
condition {
foo
(x)
}
else
{
bar
(y)
}
}
Push Fors Down
This comes from data oriented school of thought. Few things are few,
many things are many. Programs usually operate with bunches of
objects. Or at least the hot path usually involves handling many
entities. It is the volume of entities that makes the path hot in
the first place. So it often is prudent to introduce a concept of a
“batch” of objects, and make operations on batches the base case,
with a scalar version being a special case of a batched ones:
// GOOD
frobnicate_batch
(walruses)
// BAD
for
walrus
in
walruses {
frobnicate
(walrus)
}
The primary benefit here is performance. Plenty of performance,
in extreme cases
.
If you have a whole batch of things to work with, you can amortize
startup cost and be flexible about the order you process things. In
fact, you don’t even need to process entities in any particular
order, you can do vectorized/struct-of-array tricks to process one
field of all entities first, before continuing with other fields.
Perhaps the most fun example here is
FFT-based polynomial multiplication
: turns out, evaluating a
polynomial at a bunch of points simultaneously could be done faster
than a bunch of individual point evaluations!
The two pieces of advice about
for
s and
if
s even compose!
// GOOD
if
condition {
for
walrus
in
walruses {
walrus.
frobnicate
()
}
}
else
{
for
walrus
in
walruses {
walrus.
transmogrify
()
}
}
// BAD
for
walrus
in
walruses {
if
condition {
walrus.
frobnicate
()
}
else
{
walrus.
transmogrify
()
}
}
The
GOOD
version is good, because it avoids repeatedly
re-evaluating
condition
, removes a branch from the hot
loop, and potentially unlocks vectorization. This pattern works on a
micro level and on a macro level — the good version is the
architecture of TigerBeetle, where in the data plane we operate on
batches of objects at the same time, to amortize the cost of
decision making in the control plane.
While performance is perhaps the primary motivation for the
for
advice, sometimes it helps with expressiveness as well.
jQuery
was quite successful back in the day, and it
operates on collections of elements. The language of abstract vector
spaces is often a better tool for thought than bunches of
coordinate-wise equations.
To sum up, push the
if
s up and the
for
s
down!

data.title: OBNC – Oberon-07 Compiler
data.author: AlexeyBrin
data.article_summary: OBNC是一个将Niklaus Wirth的Oberon语言编译为C语言的编译器，实现的是2016年最终版本。它使用C编译器和链接器来编译和链接翻译后的代码。OBNC编译器依据GNU通用公共许可证发布，而库则依据Mozilla公共许可证发布，允许Oberon项目以任何许可证发布。OBNC包含编译工具、文档生成器和符合Oberon-2编译开发指南的基本库，以及一个扩展库`ext`。它还提供了针对文本编辑器Gedit和Pluma的语言模式和插件，以增强Oberon源文件的编辑体验。对于Windows用户，提供了一个包含所有依赖项的预编译版本。更新至0.17版时，需要重新编译旧版模块。更多文档和支持信息可从其网站获取。

• johnisgood的评论引出了一个实际应用和流行度的问题，暗示了Oberon-2可能在实际开发中并不广泛使用，这与Pascal的广泛流行形成对比。

44013671.article_content:
OBNC
OBNC is a compiler for Niklaus Wirth’s programming language Oberon. It implements the final version of
the language
from 2016. OBNC translates source code written in Oberon to the lower-level programming language
C
. The translated code is then compiled and linked using the
C
compiler and linker of the host operating system. The build command
obnc
performs all these tasks and keeps track of which files need to be compiled or recompiled.
The compiler is released under the
GNU General Public License
while the libraries are released under the
Mozilla Public License
. With the Mozilla license an Oberon project compiled with OBNC can be released under any license.
See the
changelog
for latest updates, and
MD5SUMS
to verify the integrity of downloaded files.
Downloads
The source package
obnc
contains the compiler with a build tool, a documentation generator and a small basic library of seven modules defined in
The Oakwood Guidelines for Oberon-2 Compiler Developers
. It also contains a (non-standard) library called
ext
which extends the basic library with modules for accessing command line arguments and environment variables, printing to the standard error stream, converting numbers to strings and vice versa, and for customizing the trap handler. The
ext
library was previously distributed as a separate package but has now been included in the main package for convenience.
obnc_0.17.2.tar.gz
(228 KB)
Obnc
is implemented in
C
and should compile on any
POSIX
compatible operating system. To build
obnc
you also need the Boehm-Demers-Weiser garbage collector
GC
. Further instructions are included in the
README
file in the root directory of the package.
For MS Windows users there is also a pre-compiled version of OBNC with all dependencies included (GC, SDL, Gawk and TCC):
obnc_0.17.2_win32.zip
(2.3 MB)
Note: Output files generated by OBNC version 0.15 or earlier are not compatible with OBNC 0.17. If you have used a previous version, your modules need to be recompiled; simply delete the generated
.obnc
directory in your module directories before using the new version.
Text editor extensions
To make editing of Oberon source files more pleasant I have created a language mode for the text editor
Gedit
which provides syntax highlighting, and also a plugin which automatically converts reserved and predefined words from lowercase to uppercase as you type them. These extensions are also compatible with the text editor
Pluma
which is a fork of Gedit that has a more traditional look.
gtksourceview-oberon_1.0.0.zip
(18.9 KB)
gedit-convertwords_1.0.0.zip
(16.7 KB)
Documentation
Oberon:
The Programming Language Oberon
Type compatibility in Oberon
Library module definitions
OBNC Commands:
obnc
obnc-compile
obnc-path
obncdoc
OBNC – Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
Articles
Getting started with Oberon and OBNC
Data abstraction in Oberon
Books
Object-Oriented Programming in Oberon-2
(PDF, 1.4 MB)
by Hanspeter Mössenböck
Oberon-2 has language support for type-bound procedures (methods), otherwise it is very similar to standard Oberon which OBNC targets (the article
Data abstraction in Oberon
describes how classes are implemented in standard Oberon).
Contact
If you have found an error or have suggestions for improvements you can contact
karl@miasap.se
. Questions about Oberon can be posted on
Stack Overflow
or in the
Oberon mailing list
at
ETHZ
. There is also the Usenet newsgroup comp.lang.oberon (which requires a Usenet account and a
Usenet newsreader
, for instance
Mozilla Thunderbird
).

data.author: clessg
data.article_summary:
Popcorn 是一个允许在浏览器中运行 Elixir 代码的库，通过客户端 AtomVM 运行时执行编译后的 Elixir 代码。它提供了 Elixir 与 JavaScript 互操作的 API，处理序列化、通信，并确保浏览器响应能力。本文介绍了三个使用 Popcorn 的示例：Elixir REPL、Elixir 文档交互片段和生命游戏模拟。

要使用 Popcorn，需将其作为依赖添加到 `mix.exs` 文件中，并运行 `mix deps.get`。接着，通过命令生成包含 Popcorn 库和 WASM 文件的目录，并在 HTML 中引入相关脚本。

Popcorn 通过消息传递实现 JS 和 Elixir 代码的交互。Elixir 端需要定义一个包含 `start/0` 函数的入口模块，并配置在 `config.ex` 文件中。完成 Elixir 初始化后，通过 `Wasm.send_elixir_ready/1` 通知 JS 端。

Popcorn API 提供了 `Popcorn.init(options)` 方法来初始化实例，并支持通过 `call` 和 `cast` 方法与 Elixir 进程通信。Elixir 端则使用 `Popcorn.Wasm` 模块处理与 JS 的通信。注意，该库仍在开发中，API 不稳定，部分功能未实现。
data.comments_summary:

补充讨论：
• codetrotter：提供了Popcorn项目的GitHub链接，解决了其他用户可能遇到的项目源码查找问题，表明对项目文档或发布信息中缺少链接的关注。

争议焦点：
• Popcorn项目在处理Elixir多 actors 创建时的表现问题（pesnk提出的具体代码问题），这涉及到Popcorn项目在Elixir特定特性支持上的能力与限制。

43997135.article_content:
Run Elixir in WASM
Popcorn is a library that enables execution of Elixir code
within web browsers.
Compiled Elixir code is executed in the client-side
AtomVM
runtime. Popcorn offers APIs for interactions between Elixir
and JavaScript, handling serialization and communication, as
well as ensuring browser responsiveness.
We prepared three live examples using Popcorn, check them
out!
You will find Popcorn API in
"API"
section and read how it all works
in
"Under the hood"
section.
Popcorn in action
A simple
Elixir REPL
,
compiling code dynamically in WASM.
Elixir docs
"Getting started" guide with interactive snippets.
Game of life
, representing
every cell as a process.
Getting started
Note
This library is work in progress. API is unstable and
some things don't work. You can read more in
"Limitations"
section.
Popcorn connects your JS and Elixir code by sending messages
and directly executing JS from Elixir. To do that, you need
to setup both JS and Elixir.
Add Popcorn as a dependency in your
mix.exs
â
{:popcorn, "~> 0.1"}
and
run
mix deps.get
. After that, setup JS and
Elixir WASM entrypoint.
JS
First, generate a directory that will host Popcorn JS
library, WASM, and generated app bundle. To do that, run:
$
mix popcorn.build_runtime --target wasm --out-dir static/wasm
Next, in your main html you need to include the library and
code that sets up communication channels with Elixir. Add
those scripts at the end of the
body
element in
HTML.
HTML snippet
# static/index.html
<script type="module" src="wasm/popcorn.js" defer></script>
<script type="module" defer>
import { Popcorn } from "./wasm/popcorn.js";
const popcorn = await Popcorn.init({
onStdout: console.log,
onStderr: console.error,
});
</script>
WASM Entrypoint
A WASM entrypoint is any Elixir module with
start/0
function that never exits. If you are
using supervision tree, you can write it as follows:
Entrypoint snippet
# lib/app/application.ex
defmodule App.Application do
use Application
alias Popcorn.Wasm
@receiver_name :main
# entrypoint
def start do
{:ok, _pid} = start(:normal, [])
Wasm.send_elixir_ready(default_receiver: @receiver_name)
Process.sleep(:infinity)
end
@impl true
def start(_type, _args) do
# Create default receiver process and register it under `@receiver_name`
# ...
end
end
After we finish initializing Elixir (setting up supervision
trees, etc), we notify JS side by calling
Wasm.send_elixir_ready/1
. For convenience, we
also pass name of the default receiver process. JS will send
messages to it if no other process name is specified.
We need to set entrypoint name in the config:
Config snippet
# config/config.ex
config :popcorn, start_module: App.Application
At this point, your application is ready to exchange
messages between JS and Elixir. Next, we will implement
Elixir GenServer that will process JS messages and interact
with DOM.
Elixir receiver process
This is a process that will receive messages originating
from JS. See the
"API"
section for
details on how to receive messages to JS and how to call JS
code.
API
JS
Main component is the
Popcorn
class that
manages the WASM module and sends messages to it.
To create an instance, use
Popcorn.init(options)
static
method. Options:
onStdout ((text: string) => void)
â a
function that receives any text from standard
output. Defaults to no-op function.
onStderr ((text: string) => void)
â a
function that receives any text from standard error.
Defaults to no-op function.
container (DOMElement)
â a DOM element
that iframe should be mounted at. Read more in
"Under the hood"
section. Defaults to
document.body
.
bundlePath (string)
â a path to the
compiled Elixir
code bundle
. Defaults to
static/wasm/app.avm
.
heartbeatTimeoutMs (number)
â a time
limit set for iframe to send heartbeat message. Read
more in
"Under the hood"
section. Defaults to 15s.
debug (boolean)
â an option to enable
internal logs used to debug the library. Defaults to
false.
Methods used to interact with Elixir from JS:
async call(args, options)
â takes a serializable value in JS, sends a message to
registered Elixir process, and waits for Elixir code to
settle the promise. Options:
process (string)
â name of the
process that will receive the message. Defaults
to the process name set in
Wasm.send_elixir_ready/1
call.
timeoutMs (number)
â a time limit
set for Elixir to settle the promise. After that
time promise is automatically rejected. Defaults
to 5s.
cast(args, options)
â
takes a serializable value in JS and sends a message to
registered Elixir process. Options:
process (string)
â name of the
process that will receive the message. Defaults
to the process name set in
Wasm.send_elixir_ready/1
call.
To destroy an instance, use
popcorn.deinit()
method.
Elixir
Main component is the
Popcorn.Wasm
module that
handles communication with JS.
send_elixir_ready(opts)
â a function that notifies JS that Elixir finished
initialization. Opts:
default_receiver (string or atom)
â
sets the default receiver for JS calls

data.title: Solar grants held hostage in Pennsylvania legislature – as demand soars
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了宾夕法尼亚州Tunkhannock学区计划安装5兆瓦太阳能系统以节约成本并推动教育项目。学区首席运营官Charles Suppon希望通过太阳能项目每年节省约100万美元，用于学生项目和职业培训。然而，该计划依赖于从州政府的“学校太阳能计划”中获得超过100万美元的资助，而由于竞争激烈，资金未必能落实。尽管宾州民众对太阳能的支持高涨，但该州在太阳能发展方面进展缓慢，目前在全美排名49位。区域电网运营商PJM的互联延迟和未来电费上涨也加剧了挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：宾夕法尼亚州的太阳能项目及其政策支持的合理性与实施方式

不同观点：
• djoldman认为，美国政府的许多法案常常将不相关的问题捆绑在一起，以便于直接妥协和通过。他建议单问题法案可以迫使对手在公众关注的问题上表态，从而产生更好的公关效果。他还质疑为什么多数党不更多地使用这种策略。

• koolba指出，Tunkhannock学区计划通过赢得州 Solar for Schools 项目的资助来实现太阳能项目。尽管该项目声称能节省大量资金，koolba怀疑这些数字可能被夸大，并认为资本成本可能被外部化。

• markvdb表示，太阳能已经在许多地方赢得了市场的支持，甚至在没有补贴的情况下也具有竞争力。他提到欧洲的例子，并指出太阳能的普及带来了新的市场动态和创新，如动态定价和储能技术。

• quantumfissure作为宾夕法尼亚州本地人，提供了对Tunkhannock地区的详细背景信息。他指出该地区从天然气开采中获益，并认为这些资金应该用于太阳能项目而不是依赖州补助。他还提到当地居民对税收增加的担忧，以及宾夕法尼亚州整体上对变革的缓慢接受程度。

• jsnider3简短指出，宾夕法尼亚州居民需要通过投票来实现他们想要的改变。

• giantg2质疑为何要等待州补助而不是通过融资来实现太阳能项目。他还表达了对太阳能农场环境影响的担忧，并认为居民用电与商业用电的收费标准应一致。

• roenxi对联邦资助项目的财务效益提出质疑，认为直接将资金发放给居民可能更有效，让他们自己决定如何使用。

• buckle8017认为对免费资金的需求总是很高，如果太阳能需求真的高，补贴应该取消。

• amazingamazing建议将资金给予电力供应商来安装太阳能板，并强制他们根据太阳能发电量折扣电费。

• vondur提到宾夕法尼亚州部分地区日照时间较短，可能不是太阳能投资的最佳选择。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是太阳能项目的财务可行性和资金来源，包括通过融资或补助的方式。
• 对太阳能环境影响的讨论，特别是在建设太阳能农场时的环境破坏问题。
• 宾夕法尼亚州居民对税收和项目资金使用的敏感性，以及对变革的缓慢接受。
• 不同地区对太阳能需求的差异以及补贴政策的合理性。

44022136.article_content:
A solar farm in rural Pennsylvania. Photo: Alex Potemkin/Getty images.
Published
on
May 8, 2025
By
Audrey Carleton
Share
Charles Suppon has
big plans
for the Tunkhannock Area School District.
At any given time, the northeastern Pennsylvania district’s chief operating officer can rattle off statistics about fields in which its schools excel: arts, AP classes and softball, as well as on-the-job training programs for future farmers, welders and more. Goats and chickens roam the high school’s courtyards, where students also tend to koi fish; in the hallways just beyond, high schoolers tinker with tractors, build furniture to sell and offer free tax services for the broader community.
Join our email list to get the stories that mainstream news is overlooking.
Sign up for Capital & Main’s
newsletter.
But Suppon speaks with vigor when he talks about the five-megawatt system he hopes to install across five solar arrays on the district’s buildings and surrounding property. The solar panels will heat the district’s pool and serve as the basis for new curricula and jobs training classes on the solar industry. For a rural district of around 2,000, Tunkhannock is punching above its weight class, he believes.
“We’re a smaller school district doing big things.”
Suppon’s district is in a bright red portion of Pennsylvania northwest of Scranton, narrowly outside one of the state’s more prolific natural gas regions. For him, solar is simply a pathway toward cost savings — just as natural gas, from which the district earns royalties off several leases, has been. Tunkhannock believes it could save upwards of $1 million a year by switching to solar, money that could be used for student initiatives.
“It was always a financial decision,” Suppon said. “We wanted to be able to offset our energy costs, produce our own energy and only pay distribution [fees] back to the grid.”
There’s one catch: Tunkhannock’s plan to go solar is contingent upon winning more than $1 million in funding from the state’s
Solar for Schools program
. Currently in its inaugural year, Solar for Schools was born from a bill that
faced an uphill battle
in a legislature where
environmental bills often die
by attrition — a battle that required its creator, progressive Rep. Elizabeth Fiedler (D-Philadelphia) to reach across the aisle and help marry what are often competing interests in the state — labor, education and climate.
But that money for Tunkhannock might not come through because of the stiff competition for the limited funds. While last year’s state budget gave the Solar for Schools program $25 million to disperse to school districts, the program received applications that add up to
nearly four times
that amount from schools and districts large and small, rural and urban and conservative and liberal.
“I was pleased, but hardly surprised,” Fiedler said in an email to Capital & Main of the demand.
Just 3% of Pennsylvanians now have solar panels on their roofs, though 31% said they’d be interested in installing them.
The disparity between the grant program’s budget and the size of its application pool mirrors a broader reality within the state Legislature: Despite clear and growing demand for solar energy, the political will to meet it has yet to catch up.
A 2022
poll of more than 1,300 Pennsylvanians
conducted by Vote Solar Action, an advocacy group urging pro-solar legislation at the state level, found that 65% of Pennsylvanians support large-scale solar farm development in the state. More than 80% said they support rooftop solar, while 73% support natural gas and 52% support coal.
“I [have] visited nearly every corner of the state, from Waynesburg to Bethlehem, and in every place I met folks who wanted to save money on electricity, create good local jobs and preserve the beauty of their communities,” Fiedler said.
Yet the state lags far behind most others in solar development: Pennsylvania
currently ranks 49th
in the nation for its growth in solar, wind and geothermal generation over the last decade, according to the nonprofit advocacy group PennEnvironment.
It has fallen behind other major fossil-fuel producing states, like Texas, the country’s
second-largest solar generator
in 2023; California, where solar and wind together comprise close to
half the state’s energy generation
; and New Mexico, which Environment America, the national organization behind PennEnvironment,
ranked 4th in the U.S.
for renewable energy production in 2024.
Just 3% of Pennsylvanians now have solar panels on their roofs, Vote Solar Action’s poll found — though 31% said they’d be interested in installing them.
The lag could be attributed, in part, to interconnection delays by the regional grid operator PJM — though many of its neighbors in the same system, like Washington D.C., New Jersey and North Carolina, have
eclipsed
Pennsylvania’s solar production.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI收购WindSurf及其对编码AI模型的影响

不同观点：
• **resters的观点**：
  - OpenAI收购WindSurf是因为其模型在某些编码关键领域表现优异，尤其是在处理特定框架和编程语言版本方面，这可能为OpenAI带来6个月的领先优势。
  - 当前顶尖的编码模型在处理编码细节（如使用正确的API版本）时仍有问题，而WindSurf的数据可以帮助改善这些问题。
  - 认为编码模型的基本能力是AI领域的重要机会，结合推理能力可以实现更复杂的任务。

• **antirez的观点**：
  - 认为将用户转移到较弱的模型是不合理的，特别是在有多种LLM订阅选项的情况下。
  - 对“AI内置于编辑器”的做法持批评态度，认为这限制了开发者的自由选择，使设计交互过于关注代码而非设计本身。

• **firejake308的观点**：
  - 疑惑WindSurf在被OpenAI收购的情况下为何仍继续开发自己的模型，猜测这些工作是在收购前开始的。

• **blixt的观点**：
  - 认为WindSurf从其编辑器中收集的数据非常宝贵，特别是对于创建全自动化的软件工程师（SWE）而言。
  - 提到大多数基础模型提供者可能只能依赖二手数据，而WindSurf的数据可能更直接有效。
  - 提到微软的Copilot及其数据共享问题。

• **bluelightning2k的观点**：
  -  cynical take：认为WindSurf将自己描述为全栈AI IDE公司是为了吸引投资，可能提高其估值。
  -  optimistic take：认为针对特定用例微调模型是合理的，且可能有效。
  -  bonus take：提到他们可能在利用大规模收集的用户数据进行训练。

• **dyl000的观点**：
  - 认为WindSurf拥有太多有价值的数据，开发自己的模型是必然的。
  - 提到Claude API调用可能影响其盈利能力，并提供了一个开源替代方案的链接。

• **aquir的观点**：
  - 指出其开发工作需要特定的VSCode扩展（针对ERP系统的领域特定语言），因此选项有限，只能在VSCode+Copilot或Cursor之间选择。

• **infecto的观点**：
  - 请求提供ARM Linux版本的构建支持。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及的争议焦点在于是否应将用户转移到较弱的模型以及利用用户数据进行模型训练的伦理问题。
- 不同观点对WindSurf数据的价值及其对编码模型改进的潜力持不同看法。
- 对微软Copilot及其数据共享的讨论也值得注意。

data.title: Show HN: Python Simulator of David Deutsch’s “Constructor Theory of Time”
data.author: SandroG
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个基于David Deutsch构造理论（Constructor Theory）的Python模拟器。该项目通过代码实现了构造理论的核心概念，包括任务、构造器、不可逆任务和量子任务等，并展示了自复制和构造器引导的过程。主要功能包括ASCII可视化、连续动力学模拟、引力和电磁任务等。项目提供了演示脚本和单元测试，并欢迎社区贡献新功能和改进文档。该项目以教育为目的，基于MIT许可证发布。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个涉及构造理论（constructor theory）和量子物理的编程项目（demo.py）的功能、应用及理论背景存在不同角度的讨论和疑问。

不同观点：
• [moneywaters] 关注程序的实际运行效果，提出在运行 `demo.py` 时，Matplotlib 窗口中的图像没有动态效果，质疑是否应该有动态移动效果。
  
• [canvascritic] 对项目表示赞赏，但指出构造理论在主流物理学中尚未获得稳固地位，且该领域存在较多炒作。同时，提出项目可以改进的地方，例如增加可插拔的后端以测试不同的“任务本体”（task ontologies）。此外，还建议使用范畴论（category theory）中的概念（如态射、函子、单子等）来更好地建模和分析任务和构造器，提供了一个较为理论化的技术建议。
  
• [amelius] 关注项目的实际物理模拟能力，询问该程序是否能够模拟氢原子的行为，以及两个氢原子在不同能量下的接触反应，显示出对项目实际应用场景的关心。

• [revskill] 直接对项目的目的提出疑问，表示不清楚项目的用途，反映出对项目整体目标和意义的困惑。

补充讨论：
- 用户[canvascritic] 提到了构造理论和量子引力、引力子的相关性，但指出在没有可证伪的物理模型支持下，这些内容可能只是“数学化的角色扮演”（mathematized cosplay），反映了对项目理论背景的批评，同时也强调了这一批评并非针对项目本身，而是对整个领域的看法。
- 用户[canvascritic] 进一步提出了使用范畴论来增强项目建模能力的具体技术建议，例如使用态射（morphisms）、函子（functors）、单子（monads）等数学工具，来处理任务的组合、构造器的定义以及量子或不可逆效应的建模。
- 争议焦点在于用户[canvascritic] 对构造理论的批评与其他用户对项目实际功能和应用的关注之间的差异。部分用户关注项目的实际运行和物理模拟能力，而[canvascritic] 则从理论角度提出了对项目改进的建议和批评。

constructor-theory-simulator
A
Python implementation
of David Deutsch’s Constructor Theory framework, exposing key concepts—from simple Tasks and branching substrates to quantum-gravity and electromagnetism—entirely in code. Includes a “universal constructor” that can bootstrap itself from a list of Tasks, demonstrating self-replication and the power of Constructor Theory.
“A demonstration of how constructor theory
could
be explored in code, not a high-precision physics engine. For the formal definitions, see David Deutsch and Chiara Marletto’s recent paper “
Constructor Theory of Time
” (May 13, 2025).
🚀 Features
Core framework
: Attributes, Substrates, Tasks, Constructors
Irreversible & quantum tasks
: Many-worlds branching, decoherence guards
Timers & Clocks
: Simulate proper-time, special/general relativity corrections
Fungibility & SwapConstructor
: Free exchange of identical substrates
ASCII visualizer
:
ascii_branch()
for quick text-based branch inspection
Continuous dynamics
: 1D & 2D substrates,
DynamicsTask
, RK4 & symplectic integrators
Coupling tasks
:
Gravitational two-body (1D)
Coulomb coupling (1D)
Lorentz-force (2D) for charged particles in a magnetic field
Quantum-Gravity & Electromagnetism
: Graviton & Photon emission/absorption Tasks
UniversalConstructor
: Bootstraps any list of Tasks into a working Constructor
Demo scripts
:
demo.py
– shows every constructor in action
bootstrap_demo.py
– elegant self-replication via the UniversalConstructor
🛠 Getting Started
Prerequisites
Python 3.8+
(Optional)
matplotlib
for phase-space plots
Installation
git clone https://github.com/gvelesandro/constructor-theory-simulator.git
cd
constructor-theory-simulator
Run Unit Tests
python -m unittest ct_tests.py
Run Demos
python demo.py
python bootstrap_demo.py
Note:
If you don’t have
matplotlib
, the demos will still run; plots will simply be skipped with a warning.
🎯 Usage Example
from
ct_framework
import
(
Attribute
,
Substrate
,
PhotonEmissionTask
,
PhotonAbsorptionTask
,
UniversalConstructor
,
ascii_branch
)
# 1) Define your “program” of photon Tasks
ELEC
=
Attribute
(
"charge_site"
)
prog
=
[
PhotonEmissionTask
(
ELEC
,
emission_energy
=
5.0
,
carry_residual
=
False
),
PhotonAbsorptionTask
(
ELEC
,
absorption_energy
=
5.0
)
]
# 2) Build a Constructor at runtime
uc
=
UniversalConstructor
()
em_cons
=
uc
.
build
(
prog
)
# 3) Emit a photon
atom
=
Substrate
(
"A"
,
ELEC
,
energy
=
20.0
)
branches
=
em_cons
.
perform
(
atom
)
print
(
ascii_branch
(
branches
))
# => * charge_site (A)
#    * photon      (A)
# 4) Absorb it back
photon
=
next
(
w
for
w
in
branches
if
w
.
attr
.
label
==
"photon"
)
restored
=
em_cons
.
perform
(
photon
)[
0
]
print
(
restored
)
# => A:charge_site(E=20.0,Q=0,t=2,F=charge_site)
🤝 Contributing
This is intended as an
educational resource
and proof-of-concept. Contributions are very welcome! Please:
File issues for missing tasks or physics modules
Submit pull requests for new constructors (e.g. chemical reactions, friction)
Improve documentation or add more demos

data.article_summary: Vaev 是一个实验性网页浏览器引擎，主打快速、轻量和安全。它支持部分网页标准，包括多种显示类型（网格除外）、标准的 CSS 层叠行为、@page 规则分页和打印为 PDF、所有 CSS 单位（如百分比、var() 和 calc()），以及加载 HTML 和 XHTML 文档。网络功能仅支持基本的 HTTP 和文件协议。要试用 Vaev，需通过一系列命令安装依赖并克隆代码库。该项目采用 LGPL-3.0 许可，主要由几位开发者贡献。目前无正式发布版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕自主开发浏览器项目的技术选择、安全性和长期目标的讨论

不同观点：
• **支持使用C++开发**：一些评论者（如mirsadm）支持使用C++，认为C++代码可读性强且易于理解，并指出个人偏好和项目需求决定了技术选择。同时，他们认为没有必要强制转向如Rust等其他语言。
• **质疑C++的安全性和可行性**：danpalmer和mdaniel等评论者对使用C++开发浏览器提出质疑，认为C++在安全性上存在先天不足，容易导致安全漏洞。他们提到，像Rust这样的语言在安全性上更有优势，尤其是对现代浏览器这样复杂的软件。

补充讨论：
• **浏览器开发的复杂性**：Koshima和firefoxd等人讨论了开发浏览器的复杂性，尤其是处理复杂CSS功能和网络栈。他们也提到了现代浏览器开发需要跨领域的专业知识。
• **项目的长期目标**：abhisek质疑项目的长期目标，认为构建支持现代网络的浏览器工作量巨大，超出了个人项目的范围。
• **技术实现细节**：一些评论者关注项目的具体实现细节，如throwaway2037询问代码中特定定义的来源，而sylware建议使用C99+而非C++。
• **文化和语言问题**：madmod提到浏览器Logo中的日文含义，展示了对项目文化元素的关注。
• **开源贡献和替代工具**：quibono询问项目是否开放贡献，并提到对非Chromium的网页转PDF工具的需求，显示出对项目潜在应用场景的兴趣。

争议焦点：
• **C++ vs Rust等其他语言**：围绕C++的安全性和现代浏览器开发中的适用性存在争议，部分评论者认为应选择更安全的编程语言如Rust，而另一部分则认为C++是合理的选择。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **标准化小众浏览器和网络标准**：khimaros提出对小众浏览器标准化网络标准的建议，以方便"smolweb"爱好者和浏览器开发者。
• **替代项目和工具**：有评论者提到其他相关项目如Sciter和将Android WebView独立出来的可能性，显示出对现有解决方案的关注。

data.title: Comparing Parallel Functional Array Languages: Programming and Performance
data.author: vok
data.article_summary: 这篇文章比较了五种并行函数式数组语言（Accelerate、APL、DaCe、Futhark、SaC）在编程便捷性和性能方面的表现。通过四个基准测试（N-body模拟、MultiGrid、Quickhull、Flash Attention），作者展示了函数式数组语言的表达能力和代码简洁性，这些代码能够自动生成多核和GPU可执行程序。实验在32核AMD EPYC 7313系统和NVIDIA A30 GPU上进行，结果表明成熟的函数式数组语言在性能上可与传统数值内核技术媲美，且更易于移植和优化。文章进一步分析了每种语言在不同基准和架构上的表现原因。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同编程语言和工具在并行编程和函数式编程中的应用和特性比较

不同观点：
• **devlovstad** 认为通过学习像Futhark和CUDA这样的语言，可以帮助更好地理解GPU编程的底层机制，尤其是通过函数式原语进行语义推理的能力。他还提到JAX在实际应用中受益于这些学习经验，尽管他没有继续使用Futhark和CUDA。

• **munchler** 质疑这些语言是否是纯函数式的，特别是关于它们是否允许或鼓励 mutation（突变）和 side effects（副作用）。他以APL为例，指出尽管APL允许可变状态和副作用，但在实践中这些特性可能很少使用。如果数组内容被就地修改，他认为这不应被视为函数式。

• **yubblegum** 提到了Chapel语言，并询问社区对Chapel的反馈，表示自己虽然对高性能计算（HPC）没有实际需求，但曾经对Chapel产生过兴趣。

• **DrNosferatu** 将Matlab描述为“可移植的APL”，暗示Matlab在某些方面与APL有相似性。

• **teleforce** 指出所提到的所有语言都依赖外部BLAS库（如OpenBLAS）来提升性能，并推荐D语言，声称D语言具有优秀的函数式和数组特性，并且自带高性能的原生BLAS库（Mir GLAS），其性能优于OpenBLAS和Eigen。

补充讨论：
• 关于函数式编程的纯度以及在实际应用中如何处理可变状态和副作用的问题是讨论的一个焦点。
• 不同语言（如Chapel、Matlab、D语言）在并行编程和高性能计算中的应用和优劣也是讨论的重要内容。
• teleforce 提供了一个具体的性能比较链接，为D语言的并行支持和原生BLAS库提供了实证支持。

争议焦点：
• 函数式语言的定义和纯度，特别是在实际应用中如何处理可变状态和副作用，是争议的核心。

View a PDF of the paper titled Comparing Parallel Functional Array Languages: Programming and Performance, by David van Balen and 13 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
Parallel functional array languages are an emerging class of programming languages that promise to combine low-effort parallel programming with good performance and performance portability. We systematically compare the designs and implementations of five different functional array languages: Accelerate, APL, DaCe, Futhark, and SaC. We demonstrate the expressiveness of functional array programming by means of four challenging benchmarks, namely N-body simulation, MultiGrid, Quickhull, and Flash Attention. These benchmarks represent a range of application domains and parallel computational models. We argue that the functional array code is much shorter and more comprehensible than the hand-optimized baseline implementations because it omits architecture-specific aspects. Instead, the language implementations generate both multicore and GPU executables from a single source code base. Hence, we further argue that functional array code could more easily be ported to, and optimized for, new parallel architectures than conventional implementations of numerical kernels. We demonstrate this potential by reporting the performance of the five parallel functional array languages on a total of 39 instances of the four benchmarks on both a 32-core AMD EPYC 7313 multicore system and on an NVIDIA A30 GPU. We explore in-depth why each language performs well or not so well on each benchmark and architecture. We argue that the results demonstrate that mature functional array languages have the potential to deliver performance competitive with the best available conventional techniques.

data.title: K-Scale Labs: Open-source humanoid robots, built for developers
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一家开放源代码机器人公司，致力于加速实现大规模机器人应用，并确保其对人类有益、可访问和可审计。公司提供多款通用人形机器人（如K-Bot、Z-Bot、M-Bot），价格从999美元到15,999美元不等，现已开放预订。其机器人技术栈包括硬件、软件和机器学习，集成良好，支持快速部署物理AI。K-Lang语言、K-Sim强化学习框架及K-OS操作系统等工具帮助开发者高效创建、测试和部署机器人应用。所有代码均为开源，并支持模拟到现实的无缝转移。公司已完成六代机器人开发，并与学术界（如斯坦福大学）合作推广。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Z-bot机器人相关技术细节、设计选择、成本以及其实用性和潜力

不同观点：
• bArray认为Z-bot的驱动器可能足以支持其移动，但缺乏关于传感器、计算能力、电池等关键信息的详细介绍，让人难以了解其实际能力。
• anonzzzies质疑为何要设计成 humanoid 形态，建议仿生设计如蜘蛛、狗等，或者至少像猿类，以增加稳定性和多功能性。
• v9v指出该开源机器人设计的硬件细节不足，GitHub仓库和文档均为空白，难以获取更详细的信息。
• quanto对 humanoid 机器人硬件成本的驱动因素提出疑问，尤其是关于Dynamixel智能伺服电机和 exotic 传感器，并指出尽管近年来许多组件价格下降，但具体成本仍不明确。
• awongh对Z-bot的定价感到意外，并询问是否存在同价位的其他 humanoid 机器人。
• fennecbutt表示对Z-bot的兴趣，并希望这种实验性机器人能进入个人工作坊，类似于reprap的成功案例。
• canvascritic对Z-bot的宣传持怀疑态度，认为需要实际的基准测试来验证其声称的开放源 humanoid 堆栈，尤其是关于强化学习基础设施的有效性。
• dang提到该项目之前可能已经展示过，但未提供进一步的链接或信息。
• OsrsNeedsf2P曾参加过相关活动，认为Z-bot在位置感知和稳定性方面存在不足，导致机器人容易失控。
• paulsutter表示其团队对Z-bot在工业任务中的应用感兴趣，并愿意提供帮助以推动当前技术的发展。
• whatever1对项目团队的宣传方式提出批评，认为其依赖社区设计强化学习奖励函数的做法不够实际。

data.title: Hyper Typing
data.author: azhenley
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了TypeScript类型系统中的一个固有权衡：更严格的类型更安全，但往往更复杂。作者提出一种称为“过度类型化”（hyper-typing）的现象，即一些库为了追求完美的类型安全，导致类型过于复杂，难以理解，产生晦涩的错误信息，甚至引发不安全的变通方法。作者认为，简单的类型或类型生成通常能带来更实用和愉快的开发体验，尽管它们不是“完美”的。

例如，宽松的类型定义容易理解但不够安全，而严格的类型定义如使用泛型和`keyof`可以提供编译时保障，却增加了复杂性。以TanStack Form库为例，虽然其类型安全和自动完成功能强大，但其类型定义复杂难懂，错误信息难以解读。

过度类型化的缺点包括：类型定义文件格式不佳、类型难以理解，以及因难以使用而导致的不安全变通方法。作者建议在类型严格性和可理解性之间找到平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TypeScript及静态类型语言中的复杂类型设计与使用问题

不同观点：
• **freeqaz**：质疑是否有处理复杂静态类型更好的替代语言。提到Go语言通过空接口替代泛型，但不喜欢Go。C#和Java容易导致过度复杂的类型设计。探索如Elm、Typed Racket等语言，寻找更易调试的库。

• **jasonthorsness**：认为问题不在于静态类型本身，而是API设计不佳。复杂的API设计即使有完整的类型注释也会难以使用。

• **chris_armstrong**：指出TypeScript的复杂类型问题源于JavaScript的灵活性，导致库作者难以简化类型设计。建议通过代码生成和简化辅助库来改善可读性，使用运行时类型检查。

• **nine_k**：复杂类型问题是缺乏抽象而非过度抽象。建议通过拆分类型参数和中间类型来简化设计。

• **sberens**：希望IDE能有更多类型相关的工具，如逐层展开类型定义，以提高复杂类型的可读性。

• **masto**：分享了对TypeScript的积极体验，认为其复杂性有表达目的，能帮助发现设计缺陷。但也提到某些库的类型设计过于复杂且缺乏文档。

• **dhorthy**：提到某些流行TypeScript库存在复杂类型问题，导致使用时失去类型保护。

• **Waterluvian**：喜欢模板类型和点标记路径，但希望TypeScript能更直观地表达数值范围。

• **skrebbel**：提出“Hyper Typing”一词来描述过度设计的类型安全。

• **CapsAdmin**：复杂类型通常反映底层复杂代码，尤其是与JavaScript动态特性交互时。建议在静态语言中简化API设计。

• **codethief**：反对Astro框架的类型生成，认为其导致了许多问题和类型检查器错误。

• **codr7**：分享了在Haskell和C++中尝试复杂类型设计的经验，认为过度追求完美并非总是有益。

• **coryvirok**：强调强类型的多种好处，如优化、减少错误检查代码路径、缩小漏洞表面积等，但也欣赏JavaScript的灵活性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于静态类型语言中复杂类型的必要性和设计合理性。部分开发者认为复杂类型能够提供更多保障，而另一些开发者则认为过度设计会导致使用困难和文档缺乏。
• IDE工具和代码生成器的改进被认为是解决复杂类型可读性问题的一种途径。
• 不同语言（如Go、Haskell、C++、Elm等）在处理复杂类型方面的优劣被多次提及，作为探索其他解决方案的参考。

In this article, I talk about an inherent trade-off in TypeScript's type
system: stricter types are safer, but often more complex. I describe a
phenomenon I call "hyper-typing", where libraries - in pursuit of perfect type
safety - end up with overly complex types that are hard-to-understand, produce
cryptic errors, and paradoxically even lead to unsafe workarounds.
I argue that simpler types, or even type generation, often lead to a more
practical and enjoyable developer experience despite being less "perfect".
TypeScript’s type system is
gradual
: when describing a JavaScript value with
TypeScript, you can be more or less accurate, ranging from saying that the value
could be anything (
any
), to describing in absolute detail what the value is
under different conditions.
Consider for example this function which prints the property of an object - if
it exists:
function
printProperty
(
obj
,
key
)
{
if
(
typeof
obj
===
"object"
&&
obj
!==
null
&&
Object.
hasOwn
(obj,
key))
{
console.
log
(obj[key]);
}
}
We can type it in a
loose
way as follows:
function
printProperty
(
obj
:
any
,
key
:
string
)
{
if
(
typeof
obj
===
"object"
&&
obj
!==
null
&&
Object.
hasOwn
(obj,
key))
{
console.
log
(obj[key]);
}
}
But we can also be more
strict
, requiring
obj
to be an object and
key
to
be one of its properties:
function
printProperty
<
Obj
extends
object
>(
obj
:
Obj
,
key
:
keyof
Obj
)
{
console.
log
(obj[key]);
}
The strictness even allows us to remove the
if
check inside the function,
since now TypeScript gives us the compile-time guarantee that
obj
will always
have property
key
:
//
Passing
in
a
non-existing
property
gives
an
error.
printProperty
({
a:
"a"
},
"b"
);
Argument of type '"b"' is not assignable to parameter of type '"a"'.
Having this additional guarantee is obviously desirable, but it comes at the
expense of making the type definition more complex. Not much in this case - the
type is still very understandable - but it reveals an inherent trade-off. Where
should we draw the line?
Hyper-Typing
Lately I’ve been trying out a few libraries that - in pursuit of perfect type
safety - make their typings so complex that it makes them almost unusable, in my
opinion. I call this approach
hyper-typing
, and I worry it’s becoming a trend
in the TypeScript ecosystem.
I get why, actually. I myself am often a
hyper-typer
! It’s a slippery slope:
“If I add this type constraint then the caller will get an error in this
particular case”. “I can make this function infer this type here so the caller
will get the correct type hint there”.
At the bottom of the slope you get to a place where yes, things work, and they
might also look good for the caller -
in the happy case
. The resulting types,
however, are a complex mess, and the compilation errors produced when the caller
deviates from the happy path are walls of inscrutable text.
An Example: TanStack Form
TanStack Form is the new kid on the block of form libraries. It pushes heavily
on type-safety, promising “first-class TypeScript support with outstanding
autocompletion” for a “smoother development experience”.
What the library accomplishes is honestly impressive. Just give it the default
values of your form and you’re set: now for every form field you define - no
matter how deeply nested - you get the correct type when you read or write its
value, when you do validation, etc.
Don’t look at how the sausage is made, though: you won’t even understand it.
Take
the simple example from TanStack Form’s documentation
.
Use the interactive sandbox and try to check what’s the shape of a field’s
meta
property (or any other library value, really). Here’s what you’ll see:
The
FieldMeta
type has 17 (!) generic parameters and is the intersection of
two types - each taking the same 17 generics - which is where you eventually
find its properties defined.
To be fair, after re-formatting the type definition file and staring at it for a
couple of minutes, I do start to understand what’s going on. For the
FieldMeta
type in particular there’s nothing too obscure, but I can’t help but feel that
this undoubtedly clever and accurate type definition is not actually
helping
me as a user of the library.
Cons of Hyper-Typing
TanStack Form is one example of a hyper-typing library, but as I said, lately
I’ve encountered others that follow a similar approach and leave me with similar
issues:
Badly-formatted type definition files
. This is technically TypeScript’s
fault, but I guess the issue is not apparent until the typings become very
complex. It should be easy to fix, though, just by running the files through
prettier.
Difficult to understand types
. I agree that they’re safer and more
accurate, but that’s not very useful if I don’t understand what they’re
actually describing.
Unsafe workarounds
. Getting into situations where I need to explicitly
define a type is inevitable, and when the library types are so difficult to
understand and use, I often end up resorting to casting things
as any
,
losing

data.title: The Fall of Roam
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文由Dan Shipper撰写，探讨了他对Roam这款笔记工具的体验变化。Roam曾因其双向链接功能风靡一时，让用户可以轻松构建高度网络化的笔记系统。然而，作者发现，随着时间推移，他很少 revisit 这些链接，笔记系统变得像一个“垃圾场”，而且每次记笔记时都会困扰于“该放哪儿”的问题。Roam的 product velocity 慢、移动端体验差以及社区问题等因素，也让作者不再频繁使用Roam。尽管Roam的设计初衷是解决笔记组织问题，但实际效果不如预期，最终导致作者放弃了它。

The Fall of Roam
I don’t use Roam anymore. Why?
Dan Shipper
February 12, 2022
Link copied
283
6
I used to use
Roam
every day, but I don’t use it much anymore. Based on what I can see on Twitter, and a casual survey of friends, I don’t think I’m alone.
A year ago, the idea of networking our notes with bi-directional links became the biggest thing in the
tools
for thought space since Vannevar Bush described the
memex
. Top-down hierarchies and tag systems became the
pet explanation
du jour for everything that was wrong with
note-taking
. So we all hustled on to the Double-Bracket Express determined to build our own networked knowledge graphs. But where did we actually go? At least for me—and most of the people I know—we got a garbage dump full of crufty links and pieces of text we hardly ever revisit. And we feel guilty and sad about it.
(It is a very appealing looking garbage dump, however.)
There are probably a host of reasons why this happened: Roam’s product velocity seems to be incredibly slow, there still isn’t really a good mobile experience, they’ve had well-documented community issues—the list goes on.
But there’s one main reason that I don’t use it anymore:
When I write my notes the thought, ‘Where am I going to put this?
’
plagues me every time. It’s a direct and immediate pain. And it sometimes gets in the way of me even taking notes at all. I have this sensation many times a day and it’s deeply uncomfortable.
Roam’s job was to get rid of that pain. And it did—for a while. But now it’s back.
.    .    .
The core idea that caught on with Roam is the concept of a bidirectional link. Previous note-taking systems allowed linking in only one direction: you could link from one note to another, but the note being linked to had no automatic link back to the original note.
Bi-directional linking, by contrast, creates a link from the first note to the second, and from the second to the first automatically. Roam made this extremely easy to accomplish—just by typing pieces of your notes in [[ brackets ]] you could link between notes, and even create new ones if the note you were linking to didn’t already exist.
The idea was to create a highly-networked system of notes with lots of links between them. By doing so, you could increase serendipitous encounters with old notes, and decrease your risk of losing a note, and generally get more out of the whole note-taking experience, or indeed life itself:
Adam Keesling
@adam_keesling
I've been trying
@RoamResearch
for a week now
I was not expecting this, but it's completely changed my interactions with the entire *world*
Quick review 👇
November 19th 2019, 1:54pm EST
110
Retweets
952
Likes
I believed that if I used it, I’d learn more from my experiences because I wouldn’t forget them. I’d take away more lessons from the books I’d read because I’d always have them close at hand. I’d make better decisions, produce better writing, and maybe my hair would even start to look as lustrous as Conor’s.
(Side-by-side comparison. How am I doing on the hair part?)
There’s a ton of intelligence and deep thought behind Roam’s design. But did it actually work for me?
Not really. If I plotted out the percent of my time writing bidirectional links vs. actually looking at my notes and clicking through the links in them, this is what I estimate it would look like:
It turns out that I am rarely in a position, while writing or thinking, where I want to glance through lots of old notes as a way to figure out what to say or do. Mostly that feels like sifting through stale garbage.
My most common behavior is to Actually Write the Notes. That’s why Roam needs to help me with the thought, ‘I don’t know where to put this.
’
If it does that well, it makes the vast majority of my time spent in the app a breeze. If it does that poorly, it makes my experience so painful that I want to switch systems.
The genius of bi-directional linking is that when I first started to use it, the neurotic hamster in my head decided to turn down the volume knob on the ‘Where should I put this?
’
question.
Why? Bidirectional linking is a very good story. Roam’s job is to make me believe that if I just surround pieces of my notes like this [[ ]] I won’t really have to worry about finding the note again. It’s now networked! The need to take notes far outstripped the need to review them (see: graph above), so Roam solved my problem.
After some time though, reality started to sink in. ‘I am not really going back through all of these notes as often as I thought I would.
’
My next automatic assumption is that if they were just organized better I might go through them more. And so, the question starts t

data.title: Yahtzeeql – Yahtzee solver that's mostly SQL
data.author: skadamat
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个主要使用SQL实现的Yahtzee游戏求解器（Yahtzeeql）。该项目包含多个策略来模拟游戏过程，包括随机选择、贪婪算法、全力争取Yahtzee等。用户可以通过命令行运行模拟，指定策略和游戏次数，还可以选择交互模式和显示结果图表。项目使用概率表（由`build_prob_db.py`生成并存储于SQLite数据库中）来优化决策，数据库包含不同掷骰结果的得分和转移概率。最终结果显示不同策略的平均得分，其中基于概率和难度优化的策略表现最佳，得分为89.5。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Yahtzee游戏的优化与解决方法

不同观点：
• [canvascritic] 认为可以通过SQL joins的巧妙运用来暴力搜索一个有限空间内的2-ply MDP（马尔可夫决策过程），并指出使用预计算的转移/得分表来模拟和优化轮流游戏是经典的强化学习方法。他还建议通过训练一个策略网络来近似SQL策略，从而将暴力搜索策略提炼为快速且可微的策略，并提出可以加入针对人类心理的优化，例如考虑人们更喜欢获得Yahtzee而非其他分数组合。

• [BarryGuff] 则认为Yahtzee完全依赖于骰子投掷的随机运气，不可能被"解决"。他否认了通过计算或策略来优化游戏结果的可能性。

补充讨论：
• [canvascritic] 强调了该方法作为学习预期值优化的教学工具对学生的价值，并提出了进一步优化策略的可能性，如加入效用函数。

• [BarryGuff] 的观点较为单一，集中于否定任何通过计算解决Yahtzee的可能性，但没有提出具体的论据或例子支持这一观点。

争议焦点：Yahtzee是否可以通过计算和策略优化来“解决”，还是完全依赖于运气。

Yahtzeeql - Yahtzee solver that's mostly SQL
Setup
python3 -m venv yahtzee-venv
source yahtzee-venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
./test.sh
You should see outputs for each strategy, in ascending order by goodness
Usage
python3 yahtzee.py --strategy <strategy> --runs <runs> [--interactive] [--show-plot]
Where
strategy
is one of:
random
- just keep the dice you're given, and pick a random category
random_greedy
- just keep the dice you're given, and pick the category that gives the highest score
all_yahtzee
- Do everything possible to get a Yahtzee every turn
prob
- Use probability tables to maximize the fraction of points you earn
prob_with_difficulty
- Use probability tables to maximize the fraction of points you earn, considering the difficulty of each category
--runs
is the number of games to simulate
--interactive
will show you the dice and ask you to pick a category for each turn
--show-plot
will show you a plot of the score distribution
Probabilty tables
build_prob_db.py
generates a sqlite database with a few tables:
all_rolls
- All rolls of 5 dice, with dice sorted in ascending order
roll_transitions
- The probability of transitioning from one roll to another, while keeping some subset of the first roll
level0
- For each roll, its score in each category, reprersented as a fraction of the maximum possible score in that category, and the raw score
level1
- For each roll, the expected value of each roll/keep/strategy combination, based on the sum of the expected values of each possible next roll from the level1 table
Results
random
- 84.5
random_greedy
- 86.5
all_yahtzee
- 87.5
prob
- 88.5
prob_with_difficulty
- 89.5
